note: Short-form release manifest for The Pattern Decoder. Every beat is copied from the book's own fields via design/build-decoder-clips.py -- no line is written here. Regenerate rather than hand-editing.

clips.name: Blame-Shifting

beats.hook: You drove me to it.
beats.name: Blame-Shifting
beats.mechanism: If every hurtful act is explained as a reaction to you, you can end up policing your own behavior to head off theirs. That is a heavy job nobody can do, and it keeps the real problem from ever being talked about.
beats.not_this: Honestly describing a real trigger, such as 'I was exhausted and your comment landed badly', while still owning the response.
beats.close: "I can see that I upset you, and I'm willing to talk about my part. I'd also like us to go through what happened next, step by step. Could someone else sit in?"

hook_alternates: Look what you made me do.
You brought this on yourself.
I only lied because you would have overreacted.
You know how I get when you do that, so this is on you.
I wouldn't have yelled if you had just answered the phone.
If you hadn't brought up money, none of this would have happened.
clips.short_definition: Placing the cause of your own action on the other person, so that your choice is described as something they did to you.
clips.summary: Someone does something hurtful, then explains it as your doing. By the end you are apologizing for causing what they chose to do.
misuse_warning: People are sometimes accused of blame-shifting for mentioning any context at all. Explaining what led up to something is fair. The concern is explanations that leave no room for the speaker's own choice.
Using the label to avoid hearing a legitimate point about your own contribution turns it into a way of dodging.
clips.safety_note: Blame-shifting in an ordinary argument is a communication problem. Concern rises when you are blamed for someone's shouting, breaking things or physical force, or told you deserve it, because you may then be made responsible for managing their anger. Fear of their reaction or any injury is the signal. A domestic abuse advocate or trusted person can help you plan. If you are hurt or afraid for your life, call the emergency number where you live.

clips.name: Emotional Parasitism

beats.hook: That sounds hard. Anyway, mine was worse.
beats.name: Emotional Parasitism
beats.mechanism: Depletion accumulates so gradually that it registers as a personal failing, such as tiredness or low tolerance, rather than as the arithmetic of a relationship that never balances. You may blame yourself for running out of patience.
beats.not_this: A friend going through a genuinely hard stretch needs more for a while, and reciprocity resuming once things stabilize is ordinary.
beats.close: "I care about you, and I've noticed that most of our time goes to your side of things. I need a bit of space for mine as well. Could we try taking turns, so I'm not worn out by the end?"

hook_alternates: You're the only one I can tell all of this to.
You're so good at this. Nobody listens like you do.
You always know what to say. I don't know how you cope.
I can't talk about your thing right now. I'm too stressed.
I know you've got a lot on, but I really need you tonight.
Anyway, enough about you. Let me tell you what happened with my sister.
clips.short_definition: A steady, one-way arrangement in which one person's feelings take most of the attention and care while the other is left drained, with little given back.
clips.summary: You give most of the listening, comfort and energy, they give little back, and over months or years you are tired in a way that rest does not fix.
misuse_warning: Calling a friend in a hard season a parasite can abandon someone who truly needs you. The pattern requires a stable imbalance over a long period.
Using the term as a character label for someone with greater needs, such as an unwell relative, turns a description of a relationship into a verdict on a person.
clips.safety_note: A lopsided friendship is draining but not usually dangerous. That changes if stepping back brings threats, self-harm statements, harassment or demands for money or housing. Then pause contact where you can, keep a record of what was said, and speak to a counselor, advice service or crisis line for a plan that keeps you both safe.

clips.name: Comparative Devaluation

beats.hook: I wish you had half of his drive.
beats.name: Comparative Devaluation
beats.mechanism: A comparison with no finish line cannot be won, because there is always another person who seems better. It can wear down confidence and also harm your relationships with the people you are being compared to.
beats.not_this: A person trying to describe what they need, using someone they know as an example: 'Could you handle the school forms the way Sam does for his kids?'
beats.close: "You'd like more from me, and I want to know what that is. When you put me next to someone else I can't act on it. Tell me one thing you'd like different and I'll think honestly about whether I can do it."

hook_alternates: My ex never made this kind of scene.
Why can't you be more like your sister?
Look at how well the neighbors' kids are doing.
Dana's husband would have planned this weeks ago.
Everyone on my team gets this done in half the time.
She posts her whole routine online. I don't see you doing anything like that.
clips.short_definition: Holding a person up against someone else, again and again, in a way that always leaves them coming up short.
clips.summary: Someone keeps pointing to other people who do things better, so you feel you are never quite enough, no matter what you do.
misuse_warning: Hearing any mention of another person as an attack can close off honest examples. The tactic is a repeated unwinnable ranking, not every reference to someone else.
Using the label to claim the other person is comparing you out of malice goes past what you can know from these remarks.
clips.safety_note: Comparisons alone are an erosion of confidence rather than a physical risk. The picture changes if the other person uses them to control what you wear, eat, weigh or do, or if refusing the standard brings anger, money pressure or threats. Then a counselor, a doctor, or a domestic abuse advocate can help, especially if the comparisons concern your body or health.

clips.name: Authority Hijack

beats.hook: I know what you really meant.
beats.name: Authority Hijack
beats.mechanism: You end up arguing the case for your own feelings, and simply being taken at your word is no longer on offer. Over time you may start checking your inner states against someone else's reading before you trust them.
beats.not_this: People who know you well sometimes offer a reading you had not considered, and in therapy that questioning is invited, not imposed; a clarifying question is not a counter-claim. The difference is whether your own account is still allowed to be the last word.
beats.close: "If you're curious what I feel, ask me and I'll tell you. I'm not looking for a reading of it. What I've told you is what's true for me."

hook_alternates: Deep down you want me to say sorry.
You don't actually feel that, you just think you do.
I understand you better than you understand yourself.
You say you're fine, but I can tell you aren't, and I know why.
You're not upset about the meeting. You're upset about your mother.
A supervisor's feedback form lists your 'real motivation' for a decision you explained in writing.
clips.short_definition: Insisting you know what another person really feels, thinks or meant better than they do, and treating their own account as the thing to be corrected.
clips.summary: Someone tells you what you really feel or mean, and your own explanation of your own mind is treated as the thing that needs fixing.
misuse_warning: Saying 'you can't know what I feel' to shut down any honest observation turns a defense into a wall. Others sometimes see patterns you cannot, and you can listen without agreeing.
Using the label for anyone who offers an interpretation can hurt people who are trying to help.
clips.safety_note: Being told what you really feel is a dispute over who gets to describe your inner life. It deserves closer attention when the 'correction' is used to override your refusals, your consent or your account of being hurt. If you feel pressed toward something you have said no to, speak to a trusted person or an advocate outside the relationship before agreeing to anything.

clips.name: Boundary Testing

beats.hook: It's just a hug, relax.
beats.name: Boundary Testing
beats.mechanism: Since no single step seems worth a row, the line can move a long way without one clear moment to hold it. The person on the receiving end often feels the shift only afterwards, and wonders why they didn't say something sooner.
beats.not_this: A one-off misjudgement with nothing following it, which is a mistake.
beats.close: "I said no calls after nine, and this one came at ten. I'd like us to keep to that, and I'm happy to talk about what was so urgent."

hook_alternates: You didn't say anything last time.
I only borrowed it. You never mind.
Oh come on, one more drink won't hurt.
You're making a big deal out of nothing.
I wasn't going to ask, but I'm already outside.
I know you said no calls after nine, but this was important.
clips.short_definition: Crossing a stated or implied limit in small steps, where each step that goes unchallenged is followed by a slightly bigger one.
clips.summary: Someone keeps nudging past a line you have drawn, a little further each time, so that it never seems big enough to make a fuss about.
misuse_warning: Reading every awkward misstep as testing can punish people who simply didn't know the limit. The label needs a limit that was clear and a crossing that repeated.
Telling someone they are 'testing' you in the middle of a disagreement can end the chance for them to just say sorry and adjust.
clips.safety_note: Testing is usually a matter of pace and respect. It deserves more concern when the steps move toward your body, home, location or belongings, or when saying no to a small step brings anger. Trust the discomfort you notice early. If crossings include touch you did not agree to, following you, or turning up uninvited at home, keep a dated record and contact an advocate or the police non-emergency line.

clips.name: "Managed Out" Through Exhaustion

beats.hook: We're just going in a different direction.
beats.name: "Managed Out" Through Exhaustion
beats.mechanism: A departure produced by these conditions looks, on paper and in memory, like a free choice, which leaves the person carrying the story that they simply could not cope.
beats.not_this: Restructures, shrinking budgets and real role mismatches hollow out jobs, and an employer in decline has less for everyone. A transparent change across a group differs from a quiet removal that falls on one person while no complaint is filed.
beats.close: "Help me understand how my role has changed over the last few months. Could we set up a time to talk about what I'm responsible for and what you expect from me?"

hook_alternates: Maybe it's time to think about what you really want.
You're welcome to stay, of course. Nobody is pushing you.
Don't worry about that meeting. It wouldn't be useful for you.
Your calendar goes from full to nearly empty over a few months.
You hear about a decision in your own team from a colleague, after the fact.
We thought you had enough on your plate. (As the project goes to someone else.)
clips.short_definition: Slowly removing a person's meaningful work, visibility and belonging until their departure looks like a free choice on paper.
clips.summary: Your work, your say and your place at the table slip away bit by bit, until quitting starts to feel like your only choice.
misuse_warning: Reading every quiet spell or reassignment as being managed out can turn ordinary reorganizing into a grievance. The label needs a comparison, a timeline and a lack of explanation, not just a bad feeling.
Telling a coworker they are being managed out can add to their distress or push a decision that the evidence does not support.
clips.safety_note: This is chiefly a threat to income and standing, though a visa or housing tied to the job raises the stakes. Concern grows if pay or immigration status depends on staying, if you are pressed to sign a separation agreement quickly, or if the strain is hurting your sleep or health. Get advice from an employment lawyer, union or legal aid service before signing, and keep dated notes of what changed.

clips.name: Bounded Choice

beats.hook: Nobody forced you. You said yes of your own free will.
beats.name: Bounded Choice
beats.mechanism: Choices feel entirely your own while the range they were drawn from has closed, so you carry full responsibility for outcomes you were never given room to avoid. It also makes asking for help harder, since nothing seems to have been forced.
beats.not_this: Every environment shapes what feels choosable. A job, a mortgage or a close family all narrow options, and feeling free within limits is ordinary.
beats.close: Before I accept that I chose this freely, I ask myself: "Could I say no and keep my home, my friends and my standing? Who told me the other options are not real, and have I heard it from anyone outside?"

hook_alternates: You wanted this. Why are you acting like you had no choice?
Sure, take the outside job. Just know what it says about your commitment.
We never tell anyone what to do. We just ask you to pray about the right answer.
Of course you can go to the family wedding. You just have to decide where your loyalty lies.
It's your decision, and we'll support whatever you choose, as long as it's the one already shown to you.
clips.short_definition: Shaping a member's world so every remaining option looks like a free personal pick, while the only options left are ones that serve the group.
clips.summary: The real alternatives were closed off or made so costly that only one answer was left, yet everyone keeps saying you chose it freely.
misuse_warning: Cost, family duty and a demanding career are ordinary constraints. Treating each of them as coercion erases the real decisions behind a person's life.
Telling someone they never really chose their life can take away their agency. The label is for understanding pressure, not for overriding what a person says they wanted.
clips.safety_note: Bounded choice alone is a pattern of pressure, not necessarily danger. It becomes safety-relevant when the narrowed options involve housing, money, immigration status, medical care or children, or when anyone is threatened for taking another path. Then consult a lawyer or legal aid, or a cult-recovery advocate, before acting, and plan any big change privately.

clips.name: Exaggeration

beats.hook: You ALWAYS do this.
beats.name: Exaggeration
beats.mechanism: A stretched claim is hard to answer. Defending yourself against 'never' can make you look petty for listing the one time, and a fair point buried inside the claim gets lost along with the exaggeration.
beats.not_this: Ordinary venting, such as 'ugh, you always leave the cupboards open' said with a sigh and a half-smile.
beats.close: "Hearing what's wrong is what I want, and a real example is how I can do it. Can you tell me about one time this week? Then we can talk about that, instead of always and never."

hook_alternates: You never listen to me.
You've ruined the whole trip.
Nobody on the team agrees with you.
You haven't called me once this month.
Every single time I ask for one thing, it turns into a fight.
clips.short_definition: Stretching a claim with words like always, never, everyone or nothing, so it sounds bigger and harder to answer than the facts support.
clips.summary: Someone turns a specific problem into a sweeping one, with words like 'you never' and 'you always', so you end up arguing about the word instead of the thing that happened.
misuse_warning: Labeling a frustrated 'you never' as manipulation can make it harder for the person to say anything strongly, and leaves the fair core of the complaint unheard.
Counting up someone's 'always' statements as evidence against them turns a speech habit into a verdict.
clips.safety_note: Stretched wording is an everyday habit and rarely a safety signal alone. That changes if sweeping charges come with threats, if you fear the reaction when you ask for an example, or if the same claims about you are repeated to others in ways that cut you off from them. Write down what was said and when, and show it to someone you trust before the next argument.

clips.name: Credit Laundering

beats.hook: I think someone mentioned it in a meeting a while back.
beats.name: Credit Laundering
beats.mechanism: You watch your own work succeed without you and cannot point to a moment when it was taken. That makes raising it feel like sour grapes, even to you, while promotions and trust go to others.
beats.not_this: Ideas do improve as they pass through people, and the later version may truly belong to the group.
beats.close: "The earliest version of this is my email from the second week of March. Can we put that source on the first slide before it goes to leadership?"

hook_alternates: It's a team effort, so we don't list names on this one.
Where did this come from? It's just kind of been in the air.
The announcement thanks 'everyone involved' and names the three people who presented it.
A forwarded email chain is cut down to its last message, which no longer shows your original proposal.
Great point, Priya. (Two days later, to the director:) Our team has been thinking about this approach.
The deck going to the board carries the department head's name and no mention of the analysis that came from your desk.
clips.short_definition: Passing a person's idea or work through several hands, each slightly rewording it, until nobody can trace it back to them.
clips.summary: Your idea is repeated by one person, then another, each changing a few words, until it reaches the boss with someone else's name on it.
misuse_warning: Saying 'credit laundering' about an ordinary group process can turn a real conversation about shared authorship into an accusation.
Using the label for an idea that arose in many conversations can claim for one person what belonged to many.
clips.safety_note: Credit Laundering is rarely a personal danger. It would change if raising it brings threats to your job, housing or visa, particularly from someone with power over those. In that case keep dated copies of your own work and speak to an employment advice service or union representative before pushing further.

clips.name: Context Collapse Exploitation

beats.hook: Here's what they said in 2016. Nothing has changed.
beats.name: Context Collapse Exploitation
beats.mechanism: The version that circulates is the stripped one, and restoring the context means reaching an audience that has already reacted. By then the first impression has often set, and a correction may not travel as far as the clip did.
beats.not_this: People misunderstand context themselves and pass things on innocently, believing the piece they have is complete.
beats.close: "The screenshot leaves out the message I was replying to. Here is the whole conversation. Please add it next to your post, or take the screenshot down."

hook_alternates: Comments from viewers who saw only the clip: I thought they seemed so nice.
A group chat joke posted to a public thread with the line: This is what they really think.
A cropped screenshot of one angry-looking reply, captioned: Look how this person talks to people.
A twelve-second clip of a laugh, captioned as mockery of someone grieving, with the minute before it left out.
A quote that stops at 'I don't think any of us should have to' when the line went on to say 'be afraid to ask for help'.
clips.short_definition: Passing on a statement or image without the surrounding material that gave it its meaning, so viewers read something different from what was meant where it began.
clips.summary: A piece of something you said or posted is cut out of its setting and shared, so people who see only that piece think you meant something you did not.
misuse_warning: Saying 'you took it out of context' about every unwelcome quote can protect someone who really did say it. The label needs the missing part to change the meaning.
Accusing a sharer of manipulation when they simply never saw the full conversation turns a mistake into a charge.
clips.safety_note: A clipped quote circulating is a reputation problem, not a physical one. It changes if the clipped version brings threats, your address or workplace being posted, or calls to people who hold power over your income or housing. Save dated copies of both versions and the replies, and take them to the platform's report tool and, if threats appear, the police.

clips.name: AI-Driven Narrative Hijacking

beats.hook: Dozens of comment sections open with near-identical wording in different casual voices.
beats.name: AI-Driven Narrative Hijacking
beats.mechanism: Volume settles what a topic is about before most people have finished forming a view. The terms of the argument arrive already fixed, and those who disagree find themselves answering a question they never chose.
beats.not_this: Coordinated campaigning is normal politics, and popular ideas spread fast on their own. Virality is not evidence of synthesis. Volume alone says nothing about where something came from.
beats.close: "I've seen this everywhere in a day, and that alone tells me nothing. Before I repeat it, I want a named source and the original recording. If I can't find them, I'll hold off and say so."

hook_alternates: Images or clips that look like eyewitness evidence cannot be traced back to any named source.
Any reasoned counter-argument is swamped by a stream of replies that restate the original frame.
A new phrase or slogan appears everywhere within hours and is repeated by accounts with no history.
A topic you barely heard of yesterday seems to dominate every feed today, with a single story attached.
Articles from unfamiliar sites seem to cover the same event with the same angle and overlapping sentences.
clips.short_definition: Flooding public conversation with machine-generated, tailored messaging so fast and so plentiful that one party ends up setting the terms of a debate.
clips.summary: A huge wave of AI-made posts and stories crowds the conversation about an issue until one framing seems to be what everyone is talking about.
misuse_warning: Calling a view 'AI-generated hijacking' because it is popular or unwelcome dismisses real people who hold it.
Suspecting everything is fake can leave people unable to trust anything, which serves those who want the truth to feel unknowable.
clips.safety_note: Most of the harm is to public understanding, but fabricated content can turn into harassment, threats or panic aimed at real people. If you or someone you know is targeted by a flood of fake material or by threats that follow it, save evidence, report it to the platform and local authorities, and seek help from a digital-safety or legal-aid organization.

clips.name: Ghosting as Control

beats.hook: Oh, you're still upset about that? It was ages ago.
beats.name: Ghosting as Control
beats.mechanism: With no account of what happened, there is nothing to work through. The questions stay open, and your attention stays tied to someone who is no longer answering. Closure usually takes two people's words, and here you are left to write both sides yourself.
beats.not_this: Someone who says 'I need distance right now' and then stays distant. Even a short line like that is an explanation, and it ends the guessing.
beats.close: "When you stopped replying, I was left guessing. I'm not asking you to explain everything. I'm asking that next time you need distance, you tell me in one line, so I'm not left waiting."

hook_alternates: I just needed space. Why are you making it a big deal?
A like on an old photo months later, with no message attached.
Three weeks of no replies, then: Hey you! Sorry, life got crazy.
Your calls go to voicemail, but a mutual friend says they were at a party that weekend.
A read receipt and nothing else for days, after you asked whether you had done something.
Saw you got a new job, congrats! Want to catch up?, arriving right after you mentioned moving on.
clips.short_definition: Going completely silent without explanation, then reappearing later, which leaves the other person with open questions and nothing to close them.
clips.summary: Someone vanishes without a word, leaves you guessing, and then turns up again just when you have started to put it behind you.
misuse_warning: Calling every unreturned message ghosting turns busy people and mismatched interest into accused offenders. The label needs a pattern of vanishing and returning, not one quiet week.
The word 'control' says something about the other person's goal that you cannot see from here. What you can observe is the timing and the unanswered questions.
clips.safety_note: Silence alone is not a safety signal. What would change that is attention that turns to watching: a person who ignores your messages but appears at your workplace, follows your accounts closely, or sends word through other people. If that begins, keep a dated log of each instance and talk to an advocate before you reply to anything.

clips.name: Adversarial Machine Learning

beats.hook: A company announces it has found that a system's results were being steered.
beats.name: Adversarial Machine Learning
beats.mechanism: The systems people are told to rely on, such as filters, fraud checks and screening tools, return confident answers, and the person affected often has no way to see why. If such a system has been misled, the error can land on someone who did nothing.
beats.not_this: Everyday AI mistakes. Models break on unusual inputs, carry the biases of their training data, and drift as the world changes. A wrong or strange output is far more likely a limitation than an attack.
beats.close: "This result came from an automated system, and a confident answer is not the same as a correct one. Can a person review it, and what else do I have that supports or contradicts it?"

hook_alternates: A tool that has behaved sensibly for months suddenly gives odd answers on a certain topic.
A message that clearly looks like a scam passes an automated filter and lands in your inbox.
An application is rejected by an automated screen and nobody can say which factor decided it.
A harmless account or document is flagged and blocked, with no explanation you can understand.
A researcher publishes a report showing that a particular AI product can be misled by certain inputs.
clips.short_definition: Crafting the data an AI system learns from or reads so that it gives wrong or manipulated answers, a risk to filters, fraud checks and screening software.
clips.summary: AI systems can be fooled by inputs made to mislead them, so a confident answer from a filter or screening tool is not always a correct one.
misuse_warning: Blaming every strange AI output on an attack can excuse real design flaws and hide the ordinary biases and limits that cause most errors.
Accusing a specific person or company of tampering with a model, with no evidence, is a serious claim that can do real harm.
clips.safety_note: An odd AI result is rarely a personal danger. It becomes serious if an automated tool wrongly affects your money, housing, job, health care or legal standing. In that case ask for human review in writing, keep copies, and contact a legal aid service or consumer protection office.

clips.name: Guilt-Tripping

beats.hook: You owe me.
beats.name: Guilt-Tripping
beats.mechanism: Guilt that is attached to ordinary refusals makes your own limits feel wrong. Over time you may agree to things you do not want to avoid the sting, and stop being able to tell real obligations from pressure.
beats.not_this: Honest disappointment said once, with the decision left to you: 'I'm sad you can't come, and I understand.'
beats.close: "When I say no and the answer is a list of what you've done, I start to feel I can't decide anything for myself. I am grateful, and the answer is still no."

hook_alternates: How could you do this to me?
I never ask you for anything.
After everything I've done for you.
I sacrificed everything for you kids.
If you really cared about me, you would.
I guess I just don't matter to you any more.
No, it's fine. Don't worry about me. I'll manage on my own.
clips.short_definition: Using guilt about past help, sacrifice or hurt feelings to make saying no feel like a moral failing.
clips.summary: Someone reminds you of what they have done, given up or feel, so that saying no seems selfish or cruel, even when your answer was reasonable.
misuse_warning: Hurt feelings are not always guilt-tripping. People may say how a decision affected them, and calling that manipulation can silence an honest request.
Using the label on someone who is grieving or struggling can turn a cry for contact into an accusation.
clips.safety_note: Being made to feel guilty is painful but not a physical danger. It matters more when you depend on the person for housing or income, or when it comes with threats or anger after refusal. If so, talk to a counselor or advocate before you push back, and keep the plan to yourself until it is ready.

clips.name: "Sacred Duty" Manipulation

beats.hook: A good daughter does not question her mother.
beats.name: "Sacred Duty" Manipulation
beats.mechanism: Refusal stops being a preference and becomes a moral failure, so you cannot decline without feeling you have done something wrong, and you often cannot appeal to anyone inside your own community.
beats.not_this: A person speaking sincerely about their own faith and obligations without expecting you to act on them.
beats.close: "I do care about our family and my faith, and I've thought this through. I can help in the ways I've said. I'm not able to do more, and that doesn't mean I've stopped believing."

hook_alternates: God has asked this of you, and you are saying no?
If you really believed, you wouldn't need to think about it.
It's your duty to forgive and stay. That's what a faithful wife does.
Our ancestors gave up everything. The least you can do is give up this job.
I said no and felt as if I had committed a sin, even though I didn't know what I had done wrong.
clips.short_definition: Presenting an ordinary request as a spiritual, moral or ancestral obligation, so that saying no is treated as a sin or a betrayal.
clips.summary: A request is dressed up as a duty to God, your ancestors or your family, so that saying no feels like a moral failing and not an ordinary choice.
misuse_warning: Calling a sincere religious or cultural expectation manipulation can be disrespectful to the person and the tradition. The question is whether you can decline without penalty and whether the framing is used selectively.
Using the label to dismiss anyone who invokes faith overlooks that many people feel their obligations deeply and ask for help in good faith.
clips.safety_note: This is not usually a physical danger on its own. It deserves more care when the duty is used to keep you in a marriage with abuse, to arrange a marriage you do not want, or to cut you off from help, because leaving can then risk your community and home. In those cases, speak privately to an advocate who understands your faith or culture.

clips.name: Credential-Costuming

beats.hook: I've been advising the government on this for years, but I can't say who.
beats.name: Credential-Costuming
beats.mechanism: You defer to standing that is not there, and the questions you would otherwise ask start to feel out of place. Decisions, such as money, health or hiring choices, can then rest on the look of expertise instead of anything that was tested.
beats.not_this: An unfamiliar credential is not a false one. Many genuine titles mean nothing outside their field, and a modest person may describe real experience in a way that sounds grand.
beats.close: "I'm sure it's accurate, and I double-check titles for anyone I'm going to rely on. Could you send me the name of the institution and the year, so I can confirm it myself?"

hook_alternates: A bio listing 'Doctor' and 'Professor' with no field, institution or year.
I sit on the board of several major organizations, so I know how this goes.
You wouldn't understand the details. That's why people hire someone with my credentials.
A certificate image whose issuing body has no website, or one that does not list the person.
A website showing the logos of well-known companies under 'As seen in', where no article can be found.
As a top-university-trained strategist, I can tell you this won't work. (the university has no record of a degree)
clips.short_definition: Presenting invented, stretched or borrowed titles and affiliations so that a claim or request carries more authority than the person's real qualifications support.
clips.summary: Someone leans on a title or affiliation that is invented or inflated, so you stop asking questions you would normally ask.
misuse_warning: Accusing someone of faking their credentials because their title is unfamiliar can hurt a real professional. Look it up before saying anything.
Dismissing self-taught or non-traditional experts as costumed ignores real expertise that has no certificate.
clips.safety_note: Usually this is a trust and money problem, not a physical one. It changes when the claimed credential is medical, legal, financial or about child care and someone acts on it. In that case, check the person against the official licensing register before acting, and report a false claim to that licensing board.

clips.name: Conditional Worth

beats.hook: Earn your place in this family.
beats.name: Conditional Worth
beats.mechanism: A worth meter held by someone else makes rest feel like failure and a no feel dangerous. You can end up working harder for a feeling of acceptance that keeps moving away.
beats.not_this: A direct request such as 'I need you to pick up your brother today', which asks for a task and says nothing about your worth.
beats.close: "Are you asking me for something, or telling me what I am worth? I am glad to talk about the request. My value to you is not up for negotiation each time I say no."

hook_alternates: What do you even bring to this house?
You're only worth something when you're useful.
Good girl. See, that's the version of you I like.
I'll be nice to you once you've done what I asked.
You were great last week. Today you're a disappointment.
Funny how I only hear from you when you want something, and funnier how I only like you when you're handy.
clips.short_definition: Treating a person's value as something that rises and falls with their usefulness and their willingness to comply.
clips.summary: Someone makes you feel that you matter only while you are helpful or agreeable, and that your place shrinks when you are not.
misuse_warning: Treating every disappointed reaction or fair work standard as conditional worth can make ordinary accountability look like harm. The label fits a pattern about your value, not a task.
Applying it to someone who is simply overwhelmed or burned out can turn their exhaustion into an accusation.
clips.safety_note: Worth tied to usefulness is a heavy pressure but not a danger signal in itself. It carries more risk when a place to live, money, your children or your safety is also made to depend on your compliance. If that is happening, speak to a counselor, legal aid service or domestic abuse advocate about your options before you push back.

clips.name: Confidentiality as Weapon

beats.hook: Sharing the file would breach other people's privacy.
beats.name: Confidentiality as Weapon
beats.mechanism: Being judged on information you are not allowed to see leaves you unable to correct a mistake, give context or show that something is untrue. A decision can follow that affects your job, grades, standing or care, with no visible reasoning to appeal.
beats.not_this: Protecting the name of someone who reported harm while still telling you the substance of what is alleged and giving you room to respond.
beats.close: "I accept that some details have to stay private. I'd like a written summary of what I'm being asked to respond to, the rule that limits the rest, and a date by which I can give my side."

hook_alternates: I'm afraid the details of the complaint are confidential.
That information is protected. You'll have to trust the process.
You'll receive the decision. The reasoning stays within the committee.
The findings of the review are privileged, so we can't share them with you.
We can tell you there was a concern, but not who raised it or what was said.
Because of confidentiality, you also can't discuss this meeting with your colleagues.
clips.short_definition: Citing confidentiality rules to withhold from someone the accusation, the evidence or even the source of a complaint against them, leaving them unable to answer it.
clips.summary: You are told you cannot know what you are accused of, or what the evidence is, because it is 'confidential', so you have no real chance to explain or object.
misuse_warning: Calling any refusal to share details 'weaponized confidentiality' can pressure people to break real privacy duties that protect those who reported harm.
Someone who did something wrong could use this label to paint a legitimate process as a cover-up; the label needs evidence that the substance was withheld, not just a name.
clips.safety_note: A secret process is a fairness problem, not a physical danger. It changes if the hidden accusation could lead to loss of housing, income, immigration status or custody, or if the person holding the file is also someone you fear. In those cases a legal aid office, a union or a tenant or immigration advocate can find out what you are entitled to see; start by asking one of them before you answer any hearing notice.

clips.name: Gatekeeping

beats.hook: "Send it to me first and I'll see if it's the right time."
beats.name: Gatekeeping
beats.mechanism: You need permission that others do not, and because the criteria move, there is no way of asking correctly that reliably works. Time and effort go into passing a test that keeps changing, and you may start to doubt your own qualifications.
beats.not_this: Managing access as the actual job. Receptionists, editors, registrars and records officers do this openly, and so do many managers.
beats.close: "Could you tell me which criteria decide whether I get access, and where they are written down? I want to meet them, and I can't do that if they change from one conversation to the next."

hook_alternates: "That's not how we do things here," when nothing is written down.
"I'd love to connect you, I'm just swamped," repeated across several months.
A shared folder or group chat that everyone else was added to automatically.
"Let's wait until you've proven yourself," with no description of what proving means.
"We'll let you know," followed by silence, while others got the same access right away.
"You need an introduction from someone senior," while newer colleagues are simply given access.
clips.short_definition: Controlling who can reach certain people, information, resources or opportunities, so that some people must ask permission while others get access without asking.
clips.summary: Someone stands at the door to something you need, and the rules for getting through seem to change depending on who you are.
misuse_warning: Calling every refusal gatekeeping treats ordinary limits, fees, deadlines and capacity as plots. The label needs a gate whose rules differ between people.
A person who guards confidential material for a good reason can be unfairly branded. Asking for the reason is fairer than accusing.
clips.safety_note: Gatekeeping is usually an everyday organizational or social problem. It moves toward danger when the gate controls basics, such as who may see your own money, your documents, your children or your friends, and when you are discouraged from looking for other routes. Then speak privately to a legal aid service or a domestic abuse advocate and plan any change with them first.

clips.name: Algorithmic Management

beats.hook: A manager says the system did it and that they cannot change it.
beats.name: Algorithmic Management
beats.mechanism: Consequential decisions arrive with no one to ask and nowhere to appeal, so workers adapt to a system they cannot see and blame themselves for outcomes they have no way to examine. Pay, hours and job security can turn on numbers nobody will explain.
beats.not_this: A rota generated by software is not a control apparatus. Automation in scheduling and routing is widespread and often simply efficient.
beats.close: "Which data and rules led to this decision, and who can review it? Could you send me that, along with a way to submit corrections, in writing?"

hook_alternates: Pay for the same task varies from day to day without explanation.
Appeals go to a form or chatbot that returns the same reply every time.
An automatic message says your access has been ended, with no named person to contact.
Your account is flagged and the message says only that you violated community standards.
Your hours shift week to week with little notice, and no one can say how they are decided.
A tracker shows a live score for speed, and a drop in the score leads to an automated warning.
clips.short_definition: Using automated systems to assign tasks, track output and make decisions about workers' hours, pay or jobs, with little human review.
clips.summary: Software decides your tasks, your hours or whether you keep the job, and there is no person you can ask why or push back on.
misuse_warning: Calling any software tool at work algorithmic management can overlook systems that help workers and that a person reviews. The concern is hidden criteria and no route to a human.
Blaming an algorithm can also let managers off the hook when they chose the rules; the label should not hide who set them up.
clips.safety_note: The main exposure is to income and work: deactivation, cut hours or pay, sometimes with no warning or person to appeal to. Concern rises when the pace starts to cause injury or exhaustion, so protect your breaks. Keep your own records of hours, pay and messages outside the company's systems. A union, worker center or employment attorney can advise on rights. If you are hurt, get medical help first.

clips.name: Astroturfing

beats.hook: A wave of five-star reviews posted within a few days, worded alike.
beats.name: Astroturfing
beats.mechanism: A view carries more weight when it looks like many ordinary people hold it, so a manufactured chorus crowds out the real one, and genuine grassroots voices then get doubted too.
beats.not_this: A real movement that uses professional organisers, paid staff or a national network. Organization is not fakery.
beats.close: Verification script (to yourself, before sharing): "Who is actually behind this, can I find them, and would I still be persuaded if only five people were saying it instead of five hundred?"

hook_alternates: A 'concerned residents' group whose funding and staff are hard to find.
Dozens of letters to a local paper that share the same unusual phrases.
Public comment submissions bearing names of people who say they never wrote them.
New social media accounts with few connections and a feed that pushes a single issue.
Rally attendees who later say they were paid or bused in without being told who organized it.
clips.short_definition: Making a campaign look like spontaneous public support when it is staged, funded or run by a hidden sponsor.
clips.summary: A campaign that looks like ordinary people spontaneously agreeing, but is actually being run by someone who isn't telling you.
misuse_warning: Calling every large or noisy campaign astroturf is a way of dismissing real people who disagree with you. The claim needs evidence about who is behind it.
Accusing a named person of being a paid shill without proof can itself be a harmful smear.
clips.safety_note: Astroturfing is rarely a personal danger by itself. The risk to watch for is a campaign that targets named individuals with harassment, or that spreads their personal details. If that begins, save the evidence, report it to the platform, and speak to a lawyer or a local support service.

clips.name: Anchoring

beats.hook: "The listing price is four hundred, but for you, three-fifty."
beats.name: Anchoring
beats.mechanism: Everything that follows gets measured against a figure or framing that was never justified, so an offer that would look unreasonable on its own can seem fair, and you may feel you won something when you did not.
beats.not_this: An honest opening position in a bargain, where both sides know the first number is a starting point.
beats.close: "Thanks for the opening figure. I would like to see how it was worked out, and I've done my own research on the range. Can we start from what comparable cases show?"

hook_alternates: A 'was $199, now $89' tag on an item that was never sold for $199.
"Everyone else in the family gave a hundred, but give what you can."
"The other side wants a million. I think we can get them down to six hundred thousand."
"We're thinking about forty thousand for this role." (when the going rate is well above)
"People with your experience usually ask for much more than that." (said before any figure is mentioned)
clips.short_definition: Putting forward a first number, price or claim that then shapes how every later figure and offer is judged.
clips.summary: The first number you hear sticks in your mind and makes later numbers look big or small by comparison, even when that first number was made up.
misuse_warning: Calling every opening price 'anchoring' can make normal negotiation look like manipulation and leave you unable to bargain at all.
Accusing someone of anchoring when they simply quoted a figure they believe in shuts down a fair talk.
clips.safety_note: A high opening number is a financial pressure, and rarely a danger by itself. It matters more where the stakes are heavy and hard to undo: a legal settlement, a debt payment plan, a lease, or a pay offer tied to your immigration status. For those, get independent advice from legal aid or a financial counselor before you answer.

clips.name: Gaslighting

beats.hook: That never happened.
beats.name: Gaslighting
beats.mechanism: When you can't rely on your own memory, you lose the ability to say what happened, notice a pattern, or ask for change. Naming the pattern accurately, without overclaiming, usually helps more than either ignoring it or assuming the worst.
beats.not_this: Two people recalling a long-ago conversation differently, and both willing to check a text or ask someone else.
beats.close: "I remember it differently, and I'm confident enough in my memory to say so. Let's look at the message. If we still disagree after that, I'd rather leave it there than be told I'm imagining things."

hook_alternates: You're imagining things again.
You're remembering it all wrong.
I never said that. You're making it up.
You know how you get. You always twist things.
I'm worried about you. You've been so confused lately.
Everyone else agrees with me. You're the only one who sees it that way.
clips.short_definition: Repeatedly denying what someone saw, heard or remembers until they stop trusting their own account of events.
clips.summary: Someone keeps telling you that what you clearly remember didn't happen, until you start wondering whether you can trust your own mind.
misuse_warning: Calling a one-off disagreement about a detail 'gaslighting' can shut down honest correction. The word fits a repeated pattern, not a single clash.
Using the label to win an argument or to wound someone turns a description of a pattern into a verdict.
clips.safety_note: Being told your memory is wrong is not a physical-safety signal in itself. It becomes one when it travels with threats, monitoring, cutting off money or contact, or fear of what happens when you disagree. If any of that is present, talk to someone outside the relationship, such as a domestic abuse advocate, a counselor or a trusted friend, before confronting anything.

clips.name: Divide and Conquer

beats.hook: You're the only one I can trust with this.
beats.name: Divide and Conquer
beats.mechanism: Two people who might have compared notes stop speaking, and each carries a version of the other that neither gets the chance to correct. Meanwhile no one is in a position to say that something is wrong, because each person is dealing with it alone.
beats.not_this: Miscommunication between two people that has nothing to do with anyone else.
beats.close: "If something about me needs saying, please let me hear it from the person who said it. Can the three of us sit down together, or agree that anything about each other gets checked with each other first?"

hook_alternates: You know what they really think of you, right?
Let's keep this between us. The others wouldn't understand.
I wouldn't bring it up with her. It will only make things worse.
A group chat goes quiet after one person has spoken privately to each member.
I probably shouldn't tell you this, but here's what Priya really said about you.
Two coworkers are each told they were the one picked for a project, and each is asked not to mention it.
clips.short_definition: Distance or distrust between people who might otherwise support one another, so that they do not compare notes or act together.
clips.summary: People who would normally compare notes and back each other up end up distrustful or distant, each holding a different version of what the other said.
misuse_warning: Calling every misunderstanding between friends 'divide and conquer' can turn clumsy relaying into a conspiracy story and cost you a friendship that could be repaired.
The label can also be used to cast a person's honest report of what they heard as a campaign.
clips.safety_note: This pattern is mainly about trust, not physical danger. It matters more when someone keeping you from comparing notes also controls your time, money, housing or contact with family. Signs include being told whom you may speak to, or being cut off from anyone who might offer another view. A counselor, domestic abuse advocate or relative outside the situation can help you check.

clips.name: Kafka Trapping

beats.hook: Your silence says everything.
beats.name: Kafka Trapping
beats.mechanism: When innocence cannot be shown, the person accused stops trying to explain and starts trying to survive the conversation. They may confess to things that never happened, just to end it, or lose faith that they can ever be believed.
beats.not_this: Doubt based on something concrete, such as a message, a receipt or a witness, which you can look at and answer.
beats.close: "I've answered your question honestly. If you have something specific I can look at with you, I will. Could we take a break, or ask someone neutral to look at this with us?"

hook_alternates: Denying it just proves you did it.
Only a guilty person would get this defensive.
An innocent person wouldn't need to say it three times.
If you weren't hiding something, you wouldn't be so upset.
The fact that you keep explaining shows you know what you did.
Notice how calm you are. That's exactly what someone with something to hide would do.
clips.short_definition: Treating a person's denial of an accusation as proof of guilt, so that no answer they give could ever clear them.
clips.summary: You are accused of something, and whatever you say back, including 'no', gets treated as more proof. There is no answer that would be accepted as innocence.
misuse_warning: Naming this whenever someone doubts you can turn into a way to avoid fair questions. Being asked tough questions about something that does look off is not a trap.
Saying 'you are Kafka-trapping me' in the middle of a real inquiry can sound like another dodge. The label fits when no answer could ever count.
clips.safety_note: Accusation loops are usually a conversation problem. They deserve more concern if they come with constant checking of your phone, demands to prove where you were, or punishment for answers that are 'wrong'. If you feel afraid to say no, are being watched, or questioning ever turns physical or comes with threats, contact a domestic abuse advocate before the next confrontation and keep copies of messages somewhere they cannot reach.

clips.name: Manufactured Destiny

beats.hook: You'll never find anyone who gets you like I do.
beats.name: Manufactured Destiny
beats.mechanism: Leaving stops feeling like ending a relationship and starts feeling like defying something larger, which raises the cost of an otherwise ordinary decision to go. Doubt gets treated as a flaw in you rather than as information.
beats.not_this: Two people who sincerely feel something remarkable has happened between them, and both say so in their own words.
beats.close: "Fated is how it feels to you. I'm treating it as a regular decision that I'm allowed to think about, and slow down, and change my mind on. Please don't use destiny to answer when I say I'm not sure."

hook_alternates: The universe doesn't hand out connections like this twice.
Everything lined up for a reason. Why are you resisting it?
We were meant to find each other. This isn't a coincidence.
If you walk away from this, you'll regret it your whole life.
We have been through too many signs for this to be an accident.
I knew the moment I saw you. You can't fight something like this.
clips.short_definition: Presenting a relationship as fated or cosmically arranged so that doubting it, slowing it down or leaving it feels like going against destiny.
clips.summary: Someone tells you the two of you are meant to be, and each time you hesitate that story is used to make stepping back feel like a mistake you can't undo.
misuse_warning: Calling every romantic or spiritual declaration manipulative can shame people for sincere feeling. The pattern is in how the story is used against hesitation.
Using the label about someone's religious belief in providence confuses their faith with a tactic.
clips.safety_note: Fate talk by itself is not a danger signal. Be more careful if leaving is met with threats, if you are told you or others will be harmed or cursed for going, or if decisions about money, housing or contact are taken out of your hands. Then speak to a domestic abuse advocate or someone you trust before you make any announcement.

clips.name: Contempt

beats.hook: You disgust me.
beats.name: Contempt
beats.mechanism: Anger about an action can be answered with an apology or a fix. Scorn for who you are offers nothing to fix, so it can leave you feeling lower, more guarded, and less willing to bring up any problem at all.
beats.not_this: Loud, hot anger at something you did, as long as it stays about the act: 'I'm furious that you forgot the pickup.'
beats.close: "I can take disagreement, and I can take being told I got something wrong. What I can't do is talk while being looked at like I'm disgusting. If you tell me the actual problem, I'll work on it with you."

hook_alternates: You're pathetic.
You're a waste of space.
I'm embarrassed to be seen with you.
A sneer, then 'Wow. Of course you did.'
Mimicking your accent or your whine while others watch.
Listen to yourself. Honestly, who could take you seriously?
clips.short_definition: Treating a person with open disgust or superiority, aimed at who they are rather than at anything they did.
clips.summary: Contempt is when someone looks down on you with disgust, so the message is not 'that was wrong' but 'you are beneath me'.
misuse_warning: Labeling any eye-roll or sarcasm as contempt can turn ordinary irritation into a charge. Look for scorn aimed at worth that repeats, not a bad moment.
Telling someone 'you are being contemptuous' mid-argument often becomes its own put-down. Describe the behavior you saw instead.
clips.safety_note: Contempt on its own is a painful way of treating someone, not a sign of physical danger. It would change if scorn starts arriving with threats, with control of money or movement, or with a drop in your sense that it is safe to disagree. If that happens, talk to a counselor or a domestic abuse advocate before you try to reshape the relationship.

clips.name: Burden of Proof Shifting

beats.hook: "Prove it. Show me where I said that."
beats.name: Burden of Proof Shifting
beats.mechanism: You have to build a case for ordinary treatment, and the work of proving becomes the price of asking. Most people eventually stop asking, not because things are fine but because the cost is too high.
beats.not_this: A dispute where a fact is truly contested, such as who paid a bill, and where a receipt would end the argument for both sides.
beats.close: "I've shown you what I can. This is not a court case, and I don't think I should need documents to be treated respectfully. I'd like us to talk about the request itself."

hook_alternates: "Unless you can show me, it didn't happen."
"Convince me you really need the weekend off."
"Where's your evidence that I ignored you? Feelings aren't facts."
"If it was really bothering you, you'd have mentioned it with dates."
"I need you to give me three specific examples before I'll even consider changing."
"You're asking me to change my behavior. The least you can do is justify it properly."
clips.short_definition: Arranging an exchange so the person raising a concern must prove they were harmed, are innocent, or deserve ordinary decent treatment.
clips.summary: Instead of answering what you raised, the other person makes you prove it, over and over, as though you must earn the right to be treated decently.
misuse_warning: Describing every request for evidence as burden-shifting can shield a claim that really does need checking. Some claims, including serious accusations, deserve scrutiny.
Using the term to refuse any questions about your own account turns a description of unfair standards into a way to avoid being asked anything.
clips.safety_note: The danger is rarely the demand for proof itself. It rises when the proof you gather puts you at risk, for example collecting evidence in secret from someone who monitors your devices or reacts with anger. If gathering it feels unsafe, stop, and talk to an advocate or legal aid about what safe documentation looks like before doing more.

clips.name: Manufactured Scarcity

beats.hook: This door will not open again. You'll regret it.
beats.name: Manufactured Scarcity
beats.mechanism: Fear of losing the opportunity does the evaluating, and by the time there is room to think properly the decision has already been made. People can end up committed to money, housing, jobs or relationships they would have weighed very differently with a week.
beats.not_this: A true deadline, such as an application closing date, a sale with a posted end, or a flight leaving, which can be confirmed on the organizer's own page.
beats.close: "Please show me that deadline in writing. I'll take two days to think it over. If the offer can't wait that long, I'll have to let it go."

hook_alternates: I'm not going to wait around forever. It's now or never.
I've got three other people interested, so I need to know by five.
If you leave this room without signing, the price goes up tomorrow.
There are only two spots left, and I can't hold yours past tonight.
A message from a landlord saying 'multiple viewings, decide today' with no other details.
A friend says 'everyone in the group has already committed', before you have heard the details.
clips.short_definition: Claiming that a chance, a person or a deal is about to disappear, so that fear of losing it replaces careful thought.
clips.summary: You are told this is your last chance, and the pressure to decide right now is so strong that you stop checking whether it is true.
misuse_warning: Treating every deadline as a trick can make you miss real opportunities. Check the source first, then judge.
Using the label to dismiss someone who is just anxious about a deadline in their own life makes them the villain when they may only be stressed.
clips.safety_note: This usually costs money or a lost chance and does not put you in danger. It becomes more serious when urgency is used to pull you into a large financial commitment, a move, or a group that discourages outside advice. If that happens, take the paperwork to a consumer-protection agency, a legal clinic or a financial adviser before paying or signing anything.

clips.name: Emotion Control

beats.hook: We don't do negativity here.
beats.name: Emotion Control
beats.mechanism: When only some feelings are safe to show, you stop reporting the rest and may eventually stop noticing them. What is left of your emotional life is the part that was permitted.
beats.not_this: A household or workplace with norms about how feelings get expressed, such as no shouting at the table. Cultures differ widely, and a difference in emotional style is not a tactic.
beats.close: "I can be kind and calm with you, but I can't be cheerful on command. If I'm sad or angry, I want to say so once and have you hear it without a lecture."

hook_alternates: Don't you dare raise your voice in this house.
I'll talk to you when you're in a better mood.
Smile. Nobody wants to see that face at dinner.
Look how lovely you are when you're not complaining.
You have so much to be grateful for. Why are you crying?
Go on, tell me how you really feel. (Later:) So you admit you resent me.
clips.short_definition: Rewarding the feelings a person is allowed to show and punishing or shaming the rest, until they perform emotions instead of reporting them.
clips.summary: Some of your feelings are welcome and others cost you something, so you learn to show only the welcome ones, even at home.
misuse_warning: Calling every request for calm 'emotion control' can turn an ordinary ask to lower the volume into an accusation. The label fits when penalties fall repeatedly on particular feelings.
Using it to excuse your own outbursts, as if any limit on how you express anger were control, misreads it.
clips.safety_note: Being punished for a feeling is pressure on your inner life, not a physical danger. It can change when the penalty for a feeling includes threats, intimidation when you show anger, control of money or contact, or a mood being treated as proof you are unfit or unwell. If a reaction to a feeling ever frightens you, tell a friend, a doctor or a domestic abuse advocate what happens in the minutes after you speak.

clips.name: Charismatic Authority Dependence

beats.hook: Don't ask anyone else. Ask him.
beats.name: Charismatic Authority Dependence
beats.mechanism: When one person holds truth, meaning and safety, losing their approval means losing all three at once, which makes ordinary disagreement feel like self-destruction. It can also leave a member with nobody else to check reality with.
beats.not_this: Admiring a teacher, mentor or leader and being genuinely changed by them is common and often good. The pattern differs where no second source of meaning remains.
beats.close: Before I act on this, I ask myself: "Is it true because I can check it, or only because this person said it? What would I decide if I asked two people outside this group? What would I lose if their approval went away?"

hook_alternates: Everything good in my life came through her.
If I lose her approval, I don't know who I am.
I was so afraid when he stopped looking at me in meetings.
She said it, so it must be right, even if I can't see why.
Only he really sees what's going on. The rest of us are guessing.
clips.short_definition: Making one leader the only trusted source of truth, meaning and safety, so that the leader's approval becomes a member's deepest need.
clips.summary: One person becomes the only one whose word counts, so their approval feels like air, and disagreeing with them feels like falling apart.
misuse_warning: Devotion to a teacher is not automatically unhealthy. Calling a friend's admiration for a mentor 'dependence' can shame a good relationship.
Using the label to mock a group's believers hides what matters: whether members can question and exit.
clips.safety_note: Watch for a leader who controls housing, money, documents or contact with children, for punishments aimed at doubters, and for pressure toward self-harm or giving up medical care. A lawyer, legal aid, a cult-recovery counselor or a trusted outsider can help. Call emergency services if anyone is in immediate danger. Plan any change privately with that support.

clips.name: Catfishing

beats.hook: A sudden emergency that needs money from someone met only online.
beats.name: Catfishing
beats.mechanism: Everything built on the connection rests on ground that was never there, so what is lost on discovery includes the relationship's entire history, not merely its ending.
beats.not_this: Reasonable caution about identifying details early in an online relationship is not a fabricated identity.
beats.close: "I've enjoyed talking. Before we go further, I want us to have a live video call. I also don't send money or private photos to anyone I haven't met properly, so that isn't something I'll be doing."

hook_alternates: 'I've never felt this way about anyone', said within days of meeting.
'My camera is broken' or 'bad signal' every time a video call is planned.
No friends or family who ever comment, appear in photos or can be introduced.
Life details that clash across chats: a hometown, a sibling or a timeline that changes.
Photos that, on a reverse image search, belong to a different name or a model's portfolio.
A glamorous remote job, such as offshore work or overseas service, that explains being out of reach.
clips.short_definition: Building a relationship, usually online, behind a made-up identity such as borrowed photos or an invented life story, so the other person bonds with someone who does not exist.
clips.summary: You grow close to someone online who turns out not to be who they said, so the feelings were real but the person was not.
misuse_warning: Treating every shy or private online contact as a fake identity can hurt people who are cautious for good reasons.
Publicly accusing a real person of catfishing without checking can expose a private individual to harassment.
clips.safety_note: A fake profile is mostly a fraud and trust problem. Concern rises with requests for money, gift cards, crypto or intimate images, pressure to keep the relationship secret, or threats to share what you have sent. Send nothing more. Keep screenshots, profile links and payment records, report the account to the platform, and contact your bank. If images were shared or threats made, a victim-support service or the police can advise on takedown options.

clips.name: Objectification

beats.hook: She's just the receptionist.
beats.name: Objectification
beats.mechanism: Your worth seems to rise and fall with how useful you are, so the parts of you that are not useful go unseen. When attention withdraws, it can feel like something you failed to supply.
beats.not_this: A frankly transactional relationship both people understand, such as with a contractor or a supplier.
beats.close: "Can we talk about something other than work now and then? I'll take this on, and I'd still like to know we can chat when I have nothing to hand over."

hook_alternates: Where's the person who fixes the printer?
I only call when I need something, you know that.
Don't bring your problems into it. Just do what you do best.
You look good in the photos, so you're coming to the launch.
Why would I ask how your week went? You're here to run the event.
You're the only one who can do the spreadsheets, so I'll leave that with you.
clips.short_definition: Treating a person as a tool, a body or a source of output, so that only what they supply seems to count about them.
clips.summary: You matter to them for what you do or how you look, and when that is not needed, they seem to lose interest.
misuse_warning: Using 'objectification' for any attention to someone's appearance or skills, including welcome attention, takes away the other person's choice about how to be admired.
Naming a colleague an objectifier because they rely heavily on your work turns a workload complaint into a claim about their character.
clips.safety_note: Being treated as a thing to be used is a wounding pattern, not a danger sign. It changes when being 'useful' is enforced with threats, when your body is treated as something owed, when money or housing depends on your compliance, or when you are pressed into sexual contact. Then talk with an advocate, a doctor or a legal aid service, someone outside the arrangement, before taking any step.

clips.name: Brigading

beats.hook: Report this account, plus a link, repeated by many users.
beats.name: Brigading
beats.mechanism: Volume arriving at once removes any chance of answering the way you could answer a single message, and the platform itself becomes unusable for as long as it lasts. Notifications pile up faster than anyone can read, and a calm reply is buried.
beats.not_this: Virality is not coordination: a post that spreads on its own draws unconnected people who arrived by different routes. What marks brigading is convergence traceable to one rallying post or thread, and friends reacting independently to the same post is not that.
beats.close: "Here is the original post in full, with what came before it. I'm not answering individual replies."

hook_alternates: Replies quoting a screenshot of your post that you cannot find a link to.
A run of one-star ratings on your shop page within an hour, none from a buyer.
Dozens of near-identical replies such as 'Wow. Unbelievable.' from accounts with no history with you.
Go and look at what this person said, posted in a group chat, followed by a stream of new commenters.
Within minutes of a screenshot being shared in another group, your mentions fill with replies that use the same phrases.
clips.short_definition: A group converging on one person's posts, account or message at once, usually after a shared call to do so, so the volume itself overwhelms them.
clips.summary: Dozens or hundreds of people send replies or reports to one person within hours, usually because a post somewhere else sent them there, so there is no way to answer them all.
misuse_warning: Calling any heavy criticism 'brigading' can dismiss people who disagree with you in good faith. The label needs evidence of a shared call to converge.
Accusing a named person of organizing a pile-on without a link or screenshot trail can start a pile-on of its own.
clips.safety_note: Treat threats, a home address, a workplace name or a family member's name appearing in the wave as a different level of problem from rude replies. Save evidence before blocking, report it to the platform and, where threats look credible, to the police. Ask a friend you trust to read the messages for you and flag only threats or personal details.

clips.name: AI-Driven Social Engineering (Automated)

beats.hook: A text from a number you do not recognize, claiming to be a known person with a new phone.
beats.name: AI-Driven Social Engineering (Automated)
beats.mechanism: The usual defenses, an unfamiliar voice, clumsy wording or an address that looks wrong, stop working when the approach sounds exactly like someone already known and trusted. People lose money, accounts and privacy while believing they were helping.
beats.not_this: Real organizations do phone, email and ask to verify identity, and a real bank may contact you about fraud.
beats.close: "Before I do anything, I will contact this person myself using a number I already have. A real request will still be there in ten minutes, and nobody who cares about me will mind that I checked."

hook_alternates: A 'bank' or 'agency' contact that insists on staying on the line and not hanging up to check.
A call from a voice that sounds like your child or grandchild, in distress, asking for money right now.
An email with perfect grammar that mentions your real employer, recent purchase or a family member's name.
A message that appears to be from your boss asking for gift cards or an urgent transfer, and not to discuss it.
A video call where the face seems slightly off, the audio is out of step, or the person avoids unplanned questions.
clips.short_definition: Scams that use AI-generated text, voice or video to impersonate trusted people or institutions, tailored to each target and sent at large scale.
clips.summary: A message, call or video that looks or sounds like someone you trust is actually generated, and it is built to get you to send money or information quickly.
misuse_warning: Telling relatives that all unexpected calls are AI scams can create fear and make people hang up on real emergencies.
Blaming victims for being fooled adds shame and discourages them from reporting.
clips.safety_note: This is chiefly a financial and account risk, which grows if money or codes have been sent or a relative is said to be in danger. If money or codes have gone, call your bank right away, then report the incident and warn the person who was impersonated. If someone really might be in danger, contact them directly by a number you already hold, or call emergency services.

clips.name: Account Takeover

beats.hook: 'Why do you need your email? Ask me and I'll check it for you.'
beats.name: Account Takeover
beats.mechanism: Being pushed out of your own accounts costs more than access. Messages can go out under your name to people who have every reason to believe them, and everyday tasks like paying a bill or reaching a doctor start to need permission.
beats.not_this: Forgotten passwords, expired codes and lost phones. A locked account on its own is a common technical problem.
beats.close: "My login stopped working and the recovery number isn't mine. Do you know why that happened? Let's sort it out calmly." If you are unsure how they would react, hold off and ask a tech-safety advocate how to proceed.

hook_alternates: Sent mail you did not send, or messages marked as read before you open them.
A recovery attempt is canceled within minutes by someone else approving a new device.
Your bank statements stop arriving, and the contact address on the account has been changed.
Friends ask about a post or message you never wrote, and it reads as cruel or out of character.
Your usual password stops working and the reset code goes to a phone number you do not recognize.
You are told: 'I changed it because you can't be trusted with it. I'll give it back when we've sorted this out.'
clips.short_definition: Taking over someone's email, social media, banking or cloud accounts so they are watched, spoken for, cut off or locked out of their own online life.
clips.summary: Someone gets control of your email, social media or bank logins, so they can read your messages, write as you, or keep you out, and getting back in depends on them.
misuse_warning: A locked or hacked account does not show that someone close to you did it. Look at the provider's login history and recovery details before suspecting a person.
Accusing a partner or relative of taking over your accounts because of one failed login can damage trust over a fault that belongs to the platform.
clips.safety_note: Losing control of accounts can go with monitoring, isolation, threats or control of money. Changing passwords or removing a device can alert the person to what you are doing. Work out your next step on a device they cannot see, with a domestic abuse advocate or a tech safety service, before you change anything on the compromised account.

clips.name: Agent of Influence Operations

beats.hook: A reporter's pieces that repeatedly quote the same unnamed source and favor the same side.
beats.name: Agent of Influence Operations
beats.mechanism: Audiences weigh an argument partly by how independent its source appears; where that independence is not real, their judgment is being borrowed rather than informed. Trust in real experts and reporters also erodes when a hidden arrangement comes out.
beats.not_this: Journalists, academics and executives take funding, briefings, access and hospitality openly, and holding a view that happens to suit a government or a company is not proof of recruitment.
beats.close: "Before I share this: who pays this person, and is that stated anywhere? Would I find the argument as convincing if I knew every tie they have, and has anyone independent checked the claim?"

hook_alternates: A study or op-ed that appeared just before a policy vote, with no mention of who commissioned it.
A public figure who changes position abruptly on one topic after a trip or a new business partnership.
A commentator whose opinions line up closely with one foreign government or company, with no disclosed tie.
A guest who is introduced as a neutral analyst and turns out later to have been paid by an interested party.
Several 'independent experts' who all cite the same think tank, but the funding of that think tank is hard to find.
clips.short_definition: A public figure, such as a journalist, academic, politician, or executive, who is secretly guided by an outside party while appearing to speak independently.
clips.summary: Someone people trust to speak for themselves is quietly being steered by someone else, so the audience thinks they are hearing a free opinion when they are not.
misuse_warning: Calling a critic an 'agent' with no evidence is a standard way to dismiss a person without answering what they said.
Naming a real person as a hidden agent without documents can be a damaging smear, and it often falls on those who simply disagree.
clips.safety_note: Learning that a trusted voice was steered is upsetting but not usually dangerous in itself. The risk changes if you are asked to pass on information, or if you are a journalist or researcher who is approached with offers or pressure. In that case, tell your editor or institution and get legal advice.

clips.name: FOG

beats.hook: Don't come to me when things fall apart, then.
beats.name: FOG
beats.mechanism: Any one of these pressures might be refusable alone. Layered together, they leave no kind of no that does not feel frightening, ungrateful or cruel at the same moment.
beats.not_this: Real obligations, real stakes and real concern can sit in one situation without anyone assembling them into pressure. Cultural and family norms about duty can produce all three honestly.
beats.close: "This matters to you, and I take that seriously. I'm not able to give you an answer in this conversation. Give me a day, and I'll come back to you."

hook_alternates: I can't believe you'd even consider saying no.
I'd hate to see what happens if you walk away from this.
After all I've done for you, I think I'm owed this one thing.
Everyone else managed to do their part. What's wrong with you?
I'm not threatening you. I'm just saying how things tend to go.
I've never asked for anything, and now you want to turn me down?
clips.short_definition: Fear, a sense of what is owed, and guilt layered together around a request until refusing feels frightening, ungrateful and cruel all at once.
clips.summary: When you think about saying no, you feel scared of what might happen, in debt for what you owe, and guilty for even considering it, all at once.
misuse_warning: Naming FOG for any family request that carries some worry, duty and guilt can turn ordinary closeness into a verdict on the relationship.
