A chatbot that answers a cancel request by offering another discount, repeatedly.
A cancel link buried under several menus, or replaced with 'call us during business hours'.
A page that shows you different urgency messages from what a friend sees for the same item.
A pop-up asking for your contacts or location with only 'Allow' or 'Maybe later' as options.
clips.short_definition: Interface designs that push people toward purchases, data sharing or consent they did not intend, and that adjust to each user's apparent weaknesses.
clips.summary: Apps and websites sometimes set up screens so you agree, buy or share more than you meant to, and some now adjust the screen to what works on you in particular.
misuse_warning: Calling every upsell a dark pattern ignores honest businesses that simply want to sell something and show the options clearly.
Blaming people who clicked can hide the fact that a screen was arranged to produce that click.
clips.safety_note: This is mainly a consumer harm, but it becomes more serious when it takes money from someone who cannot afford it, targets children, or collects location or contact data that could be used against them. Gather statements and screenshots, contact your bank or card issuer, and ask a consumer advocate or legal aid for help.

clips.name: Legal Abuse (Post-Separation)

beats.hook: You'll be hearing from my lawyer, again.
beats.name: Legal Abuse (Post-Separation)
beats.mechanism: Each filing looks procedurally normal on its own, so the cost builds in money, time and nerves without producing one moment anyone would call abuse. Meanwhile the person responding may risk their home, income or time with their children if a deadline is missed.
beats.not_this: Complicated separations legitimately need many legal steps, such as valuing a business, settling property or setting a parenting plan across several courts.
beats.close: "Anything about the schedule or what has changed, we can talk about directly. For the court matters, could we go through our lawyers, or a mediator, so that everything is in writing and nothing is missed?" Raise this through your lawyer, and only after an advocate or lawyer agrees.

hook_alternates: Another subpoena for records you already provided.
A request to re-hear the finances already settled in the agreement.
I'm only doing what's best for the kids, said with each new filing.
A filing that accuses you of contempt over a minor, late exchange time.
Papers delivered the week of your move, with a hearing set two weeks out.
A fourth motion to change the parenting schedule in a year, citing no new events.
clips.short_definition: Using court filings, motions and hearings after a separation, over and over, in ways that drain the other person's money, time and stability.
clips.summary: After a split, someone keeps taking the other person back to court, with filings that look normal one by one, until the cost in money and nerves is the harm.
misuse_warning: Calling a hard-fought custody case legal abuse can dismiss a parent with a real concern about a child's safety. Courts need to hear those.
Reading a hostile lawyer's letter, or a motion you disagree with, as proof of a campaign can harden a case that might have settled.
clips.safety_note: Concern grows when filings sit alongside threats, danger to a child, or the chance of losing your home, income or custody time at the next hearing. Courts also hear true accounts of danger, so a filing is not proof of abuse. Bring the full file to a family law attorney or legal aid advocate and ask what limits or protections your court offers.

clips.name: Strategic Leaking

beats.hook: A headline citing 'a person familiar with the matter' just before a major vote.
beats.name: Strategic Leaking
beats.mechanism: Information that seems to have escaped carries extra credibility, because people assume nobody would choose to reveal it. A placed story can be read as an exposed one, and readers may never learn who benefited from the timing.
beats.not_this: Genuine whistleblowing, where someone discloses wrongdoing at personal risk. From outside it can look the same, so the label should never be used to wave it away.
beats.close: "Before I pass this on: who is the original source, who gains if I believe it, and has anyone with nothing to gain confirmed it? If I can't answer those, I'll wait."

hook_alternates: A leaked memo that conveniently makes the sources' own side look reasonable and decisive.
Several outlets report the same insider detail on the same morning, with matching wording.
A damaging story about a rival lands on the day a different embarrassing story is breaking.
An official publicly 'declines to comment' while the account keeps circulating, unchallenged.
A document appears online with no explanation of where it came from, and is quoted everywhere within hours.
clips.short_definition: Releasing sensitive information through channels that look unauthorized, so that a planned disclosure reads as a secret that escaped.
clips.summary: A story arrives as if someone slipped out a secret, but the release may have been planned and may serve the people who let it out.
misuse_warning: Calling a story 'just a leak' can become a way to dismiss real disclosures of wrongdoing. Whether a claim is true and whether it was placed are separate questions.
Accusing a named reporter or source of planting a story without evidence is itself a smear.
clips.safety_note: Reading a leaked story is not a danger in itself. Risk appears when a leak names private individuals, exposes their addresses or workplaces, or invites a pile-on. In that case do not share it further, report it to the platform, and tell the people named so they can protect themselves.

clips.name: Aftercare Control

beats.hook: One day you'll thank me for it.
beats.name: Aftercare Control
beats.mechanism: If a painful event gets renamed as help, you lose the word for what you went through. Without that word it is hard to ask for change, and gratitude ends up expected where an apology was owed.
beats.not_this: A parent explaining why a curfew exists while also saying 'I know it felt unfair.' The reason and the hurt are both allowed to stand.
beats.close: "I know you believe that was for my benefit, and I'm not asking you to take your reasons back. I just need you to hear that it hurt me, and I won't be thanking anyone for it."

hook_alternates: I only did that because I care about you.
Nobody else would have taken the trouble.
You call that hurtful? I was helping you.
Be grateful someone was willing to be honest with you.
If I hadn't pushed you like that, you'd still be stuck.
It wasn't punishment. It was discipline, and you needed it.
clips.short_definition: Recasting a hurtful act as a kindness after it happened, so the person who was hurt begins to doubt their own memory of the harm.
clips.summary: Something hurt you. Afterward you are told it was really for your benefit and you should be grateful, until you question whether it was harmful at all.
misuse_warning: Not every explanation of a difficult decision is a cover story. A person who gives reasons and accepts that the result hurt you is doing the opposite.
Using the label to refuse every hard conversation about past choices can block honest context you might actually want.
clips.safety_note: Retelling harm as help matters more when the harm was physical, or when it comes with fear of what happens if you disagree. If the event involved force, threats or being kept somewhere, write down what happened in your own words, with dates, and take it to a counselor or advocate who can hear it without the 'for your own good' lens.

clips.name: Financial Dependence by Design

beats.hook: Why would you need your own account? Ours is fine.
beats.name: Financial Dependence by Design
beats.mechanism: Leaving becomes a question of survival and not of judgment, so whatever you conclude about the relationship, the conclusion cannot change anything. Fear about housing, food and children can keep a person in place for years.
beats.not_this: A household that divides earning and caring by shared agreement, where each person understands the money and can reach it.
beats.close: "Could you show me how our bills and accounts work, so I can help keep track of them? Sometime when it suits you is fine." If a question about money has caused trouble before, hold off and speak to an advocate.

hook_alternates: You don't need to work. I'll take care of everything.
Receipts, please. I want to see where every dollar went.
Don't worry about the bills. It's too complicated for you.
If you take that course, who is going to look after the house?
My card was declined and I realized I didn't know which accounts I was on.
clips.short_definition: Arranging money, work and access to accounts so that one person cannot manage without the other, whatever either of them feels about the relationship.
clips.summary: Money, work and accounts are set up so that you could not support yourself if you left, and steps toward your own income or knowledge are discouraged.
misuse_warning: Describing every division of household income as a trap can insult people who chose it freely and dismiss real caregiving work. Ask who can see the money and what happens when you try to change it.
Telling someone in this position to simply earn their own money overlooks the obstacles that may be in the way and can add shame.
clips.safety_note: Watch for money being used to control where you go, threats to cut off housing, food or children's needs, debts placed in your name without your knowledge, or fear when you ask about finances. A domestic violence advocate can plan privately with you, including how to build savings and records safely. Ask the advocate which phone and email are safe to use for that first contact.

clips.name: Learned Helplessness

beats.hook: You can't survive without me.
beats.name: Learned Helplessness
beats.mechanism: Abilities shrink when they go unused. If you are told often enough that you cannot manage, you may stop trying, and then the lack of practice looks like proof that they were right.
beats.not_this: Honest worry about one specific, real limit, such as a medical condition or a lack of experience with a task, stated once and with offers to help you learn.
beats.close: "I know you worry about me. I would like to handle the electricity bill this month, and afterward we can look at how it went."

hook_alternates: You'd fall apart in a week on your own.
I'm only doing this because I know you can't.
Let me handle the bank. You'll only get it wrong.
Nobody else would put up with how scattered you are.
Remember what happened last time you tried? Exactly.
You know you can't drive on the motorway. Just stay home.
clips.short_definition: Repeatedly telling someone they could not cope alone, until they start to believe it and stop trying.
clips.summary: Someone keeps telling you that you cannot cope alone, and takes tasks off your hands, until you stop trusting your own ability to manage.
misuse_warning: Using this label for a caregiver who is helping someone who truly cannot do a task can shame people who are doing difficult, loving work.
Applying it to anyone who ever expresses worry makes ordinary concern look like control. The test is breadth and repetition, not a single warning.
clips.safety_note: Watch for the claim of incapacity coming together with control of your money, documents, phone, transport or contact with others, or with fear of what happens if you try something alone. These can signal coercive control. A domestic abuse advocate or legal aid service can help you plan privately, including how to keep copies of key papers safe.

clips.name: Clinical Tone Policing

beats.hook: Let's not catastrophize.
beats.name: Clinical Tone Policing
beats.mechanism: When a person with training and a title calls a worry excessive, you may drop it, even when it was reasonable, and it may then go unexamined. The label can also stay in your records and shape how the next person reads you.
beats.not_this: A clinician gently pointing out that a worry has grown larger than the evidence supports, while still examining the thing worried about.
beats.close: "I sound upset, and I am. My worry is real and I would like it looked at. Could we go through what I described, one thing at a time, and could you note it in my record as I've said it?"

hook_alternates: That sounds like health anxiety.
You seem to be very emotional today.
I think you're reading far too much into this.
You're being a bit dramatic about your symptoms.
Try to take the emotion out of this and stick to the facts.
I can see you're quite worked up. Let's calm down before we talk about the pain.
clips.short_definition: Responding to a person's report of pain, fear or distress by judging how they express it, as 'dramatic' or 'catastrophizing', instead of addressing what they reported.
clips.summary: You describe something worrying and are told you are being dramatic, so the conversation becomes about how you are acting instead of what you reported.
misuse_warning: A professional's honest view that a fear is out of proportion is not automatically tone policing, and using the label to reject all reassurance can keep someone from relief they could accept.
Used as a verdict on a particular clinician after one brisk visit, the label can overlook an overloaded schedule.
clips.safety_note: Tone policing in a clinic is not a coercion signal by itself, but a dismissed symptom can be an urgent one. Sudden chest pain, trouble breathing, weakness on one side, a severe headache unlike others, or thoughts of harming yourself need prompt care whatever anyone says about your manner. Go to an emergency department for those, and if you are sent home, ask a nurse or patient advocate to note that you asked to be examined.

clips.name: Reputation Laundering

beats.hook: He's got a reputation, so I'd keep your distance.
beats.name: Reputation Laundering
beats.mechanism: The target has to argue against a portrayal with no traceable origin, while each person repeating it treats everyone else's repetition as their evidence for it. You cannot rebut a source that has vanished.
beats.not_this: Reputations are often earned. 'Everyone says that' is sometimes simply true.
beats.close: "I'd like to deal with what actually happened. If you saw something, tell me what it was. If you only heard it from others, please don't pass it on as fact, and I'm glad to answer anything you want to ask me directly."

hook_alternates: Ask anyone in the department. They'll tell you the same thing.
It doesn't matter where it started. The reputation is what it is.
Three different people warned me about you before I even met you.
That's just what people say about him, there must be something to it.
I don't know the details, but everyone says she's difficult to work with.
I heard it from someone who heard it from the team, so I assume it's true.
clips.short_definition: Passing a damaging or flattering claim about a person through enough retellings that it loses its source and starts to feel like common knowledge.
clips.summary: A story about someone gets passed around until nobody remembers who started it, and then people treat it as fact because so many have repeated it.
misuse_warning: Calling a legitimate warning from several people 'laundering' can wave away real concerns about someone's conduct.
The label should not be used to demand that others stay silent about their own first-hand experience.
clips.safety_note: Reputation laundering is usually painful but not dangerous. It becomes serious when the rumor costs you your job, housing, custody or standing in a community, or when it is used to justify harassment. Keep dated records and screenshots, and take them to an employment adviser, a union rep or legal aid service.

clips.name: Post-Truth Epistemic Manipulation

beats.hook: That's your truth; here's mine.
beats.name: Post-Truth Epistemic Manipulation
beats.mechanism: When nothing can be known, nothing can be checked, and someone left doubting everything has no ground from which to object to anything. They may also fall back on whoever sounds most certain, or on their own group.
beats.not_this: Distrust of institutions is often earned, and saying that reporting has bias or uncertainty is honesty. The difference lies between doubting a particular claim and abandoning the idea that claims can be tested at all.
beats.close: "I can doubt this one claim without doubting everything. What would settle it, who has checked it, and have I read the original? If I cannot tell, I will say I do not know instead of pretending I do."

hook_alternates: Checking a claim is mocked as naive.
Nobody can really know what happened, so why bother?
Accused of a lie, a speaker answers that everybody lies.
The media lies, the experts lie, the other side lies; it is all just spin.
A real document dismissed as 'fake' with no reason given beyond who published it.
A dozen conflicting explanations of one event pushed at once, none withdrawn when disproved.
clips.short_definition: Wearing down belief that facts can be established at all, until people stop trusting any source and claims cannot be held to account.
clips.summary: People are pushed to feel that no one can know what is true, so they stop checking and stop objecting. Honest doubt about one claim is different; this is giving up on checking.
misuse_warning: Calling a person's honest doubt 'post-truth' can be used to shut down legitimate criticism of institutions.
Using the label for views you simply disagree with turns a description of a method into a way of saying your opponents do not care about facts.
clips.safety_note: Post-truth pressure is usually not a physical danger. It matters for safety when doubt about everything leads people to ignore real warnings, such as medical, weather or financial ones. If a decision touches your health, money or home, check with a doctor, an official emergency channel or a trusted professional, not only your feed.

clips.name: Pre-Punishment

beats.hook: "There's no point applying. They would only laugh."
beats.name: Pre-Punishment
beats.mechanism: Opportunities close before anyone else has the chance to refuse them. The cost, which includes jobs not applied for and things not said, stays invisible because nothing happened, and your life can narrow without anyone noticing.
beats.not_this: A realistic judgment that the odds are poor, such as not applying for a job whose requirements you clearly do not meet.
beats.close: "I notice I am talking myself out of this before anyone has said a word. That is an old habit, not today's facts. I am going to send the application and see what really happens."

hook_alternates: "I'd rather not send it. Then no one can say it is bad."
"If I speak up in the meeting, they will tear it apart."
Writing an email, rereading it eleven times and deleting it.
"Who do I think I am?" (in your own voice, before you have done anything)
"If I do well, they will expect more, and then I will be punished when I cannot keep it up."
clips.short_definition: Shutting yourself down before anyone else can, by not applying, speaking or trying, because past experience taught you that being seen gets punished.
clips.summary: You turn yourself down before anyone else gets the chance. You do not apply, speak or try, because it once felt dangerous to be noticed, and not trying feels safer.
misuse_warning: Naming someone else's hesitation as 'pre-punishment' can dismiss a reasonable decision they made for sound reasons.
Treating all caution as an old wound can push a person to take risks that are not safe for them.
clips.safety_note: Holding yourself back is a painful pattern but not by itself a danger. It deserves more care if it comes with hopelessness, thoughts of self-harm, or if you still live or work where being visible really is punished. In that case, talk to a counselor, a doctor or a crisis line, and think about what makes your present situation safe.

clips.name: Frame Control

beats.hook: Let's be honest, this is basically abandonment.
beats.name: Frame Control
beats.mechanism: An accurate account can come out sounding irrelevant, because the terms were set to leave it out before you spoke. You arrive with a concern about something that happened and leave defending your mood or motives, with your original point never refused and never answered.
beats.not_this: Disagreeing in good faith about what the real issue is happens constantly, and both readings can have merit.
beats.close: "I notice we've moved from what I asked to how I'm asking. Could you tell me in one sentence what you make of the canceled plans? Then I'll gladly hear what's on your mind."

hook_alternates: Do you hear yourself? That's the real issue here.
I think what you need to ask yourself is why this bothers you so much.
This isn't about the dishes. This is about how unstable you've been lately.
So now I'm the kind of person who would cheat. Is that what you think of me?
We're not talking about what I said, we're talking about the way you took it.
Your email asks about the missed payment, and the reply is two paragraphs on how hostile your tone was, with nothing on the payment.
clips.short_definition: Deciding what a conversation is about, through loaded labels or topic swaps, so that your actual concern has no place to land.
clips.summary: The conversation keeps getting redefined as being about something else, often about you, so what you actually wanted to say never gets answered.
misuse_warning: Calling it frame control whenever a talk changes topic punishes ordinary drift and hides the times you changed the subject yourself.
Used as an accusation, 'you're controlling the frame' can itself replace the other person's concern, which is the move it describes.
clips.safety_note: A conversation where someone else sets the terms is a conversation problem, not a danger sign. The picture changes if raising a concern starts to bring threats, punishments, or talk of your mental state to doctors or relatives. If that happens, note what was said and when, and talk to a counselor or advocate you trust before the next conversation about it.

clips.name: Silent Coalitions

beats.hook: People who are friendly one-on-one are distant in a group.
beats.name: Silent Coalitions
beats.mechanism: There is no incident to point at, only a consistent absence, which turns the search for an explanation inward. The person ends up blaming themselves for something nobody will admit to.
beats.not_this: Social anxiety can produce the same feeling with nothing at all behind it, and some groups are simply less inclusive as a general dynamic rather than towards one individual.
beats.close: "I've noticed I'm often out of the loop on plans, and it's been weighing on me. I'm not blaming anyone. I'd just like to be included, and I'd welcome hearing if there is something I'm missing."

hook_alternates: Plans mentioned on Monday that you learn about only after they happened.
A group chat that quietly moves to a new thread without you, and no one mentions it.
Replies to your messages that are polite but shorter and later than the replies others get.
When you ask whether something is going on, several people say 'no, of course not' in similar words.
Your suggestions in meetings get a pause, then the same idea is picked up when someone else says it.
clips.short_definition: A group quietly agreeing, without any open discussion, to keep one person on the margins so that no clear incident ever exists.
clips.summary: A group keeps one person on the edge through lots of small, hard-to-prove moments, so the person starts to think the problem must be them.
misuse_warning: Treating every unreturned message as a coalition can turn ordinary social drift into a story of persecution and push away people who are not hostile.
Telling others that a group is conspiring against you, without evidence, can itself damage relationships that might have recovered.
clips.safety_note: Group exclusion hurts, but it rarely creates physical danger. It changes if the group's silence follows you into your home, your job or online spaces through threats, rumors that could cost you work or housing, or sharing of private images. At that point, save evidence and speak to a trusted person, an employer's process or a local support service.

clips.name: Deflection

beats.hook: Why are you bringing this up now?
beats.name: Deflection
beats.mechanism: The original concern never gets a direct reply, so it stays open while the conversation ends looking as though it happened. The person who raised it is left unsure whether they were heard at all.
beats.not_this: Someone overwhelmed who asks for a pause and does come back, or a person who misheard the question and answered something nearby. Dealing with a truly urgent related matter first is also fine, so long as the original topic is picked up again.
beats.close: "I'd like to go back to my first question before we move on, because I don't think I've had an answer yet. If you need time, tell me when you'll reply, and I'll hold off until then."

hook_alternates: Here we go again. You always have to start something.
That's not the point. The point is how you brought it up.
Did you cancel the appointment? / Why are you always checking up on me?
Can we talk about this later? (said again each time, with no later arriving)
Speaking of which, did you ever call your mother back? (in the middle of your question)
Three subjects in two minutes, and each time you go back to your first point, a fourth begins.
When you ask about last month's missed payment, the talk turns to something you said at Christmas.
clips.short_definition: Steering a conversation away from the issue that was raised, so the concern never gets a direct answer.
clips.summary: You ask a straight question and get a different topic, a question back, an old argument, or a stream of subjects. When the talk ends, your question is still unanswered.
misuse_warning: Calling a pause or a topic change deflection can punish someone for being overwhelmed. If you need an answer right now, check whether time is part of the request.
The label can turn into a demand for a reply to every question. Nobody owes an answer on everything, especially private matters.
clips.safety_note: Not a safety matter in itself. That changes when the question being avoided carries real stakes, like where money went, a medical decision, a child's wellbeing or a threat that was made, and raising it brings anger or fear. Then write down the question and what happened when you asked, and talk to a counselor or advocate before pressing it again.

clips.name: Silent Treatment

beats.hook: Don't speak to me. You know what you did.
beats.name: Silent Treatment
beats.mechanism: Being frozen out hurts in a way the body treats as real pain. The open-ended wait can leave you desperate to end it at any cost. Ordinary things like a reply or basic warmth turn into rewards, and the issue itself is never resolved.
beats.not_this: Saying 'I'm too angry to talk about this right now. Can we pick it up after dinner?', which has a reason and a return time.
beats.close: "If you're upset, I'll listen, and I do want to hear it. If you need time, could you tell me roughly how long, so we can pick it up then?"

hook_alternates: Talking to the dog and the kids but never to you.
I'm not talking to you until you admit what you did.
Nothing. No reply for two days after you asked a question.
Messages read, with no answer, while they chat happily with others.
A flat 'fine' and a walk out of the room, then no words for the evening.
A partner who stops sharing the plan for the week, or the state of the shared accounts, after you disagreed.
No reply to texts for two days after you said no to something, then a cheerful message once you changed your mind.
clips.short_definition: Withholding all communication, warmth or answers from someone, with no stated end, until they apologize or give way to what the other person wants.
clips.summary: Someone stops talking to you, or takes away warmth and information, with no end in sight, until you apologize or give in. The quiet itself is the pressure.
misuse_warning: Needing space is healthy and many people go quiet from overwhelm, so labeling any pause as the silent treatment can punish someone for self-regulating, especially someone with a shutdown response.
Demanding an immediate response and then calling its absence abuse can become a form of pressure of its own.
clips.safety_note: Silence alone is painful pressure, not a physical threat. It matters more when you depend on the person for housing, money or care and the freeze cuts off practical information, or when it alternates with intimidation. Keep copies of your identity papers and account details somewhere private, and speak to a domestic abuse advocate or legal aid about your options.

clips.name: Scapegoating

beats.hook: We found the problem. It's Priya.
beats.name: Scapegoating
beats.mechanism: One person absorbs consequences out of proportion to a collective failure, and the conditions that produced it stay exactly as they were, because the matter has been declared solved. The person blamed can lose standing, income or belonging, while the same problem waits for the next name.
beats.not_this: A case where one person did make the consequential mistake.
beats.close: "I'm willing to answer for the part that was mine. I'd like the decisions made above and alongside me to be looked at in the same review, and I'd like to see the findings before they are shared."

hook_alternates: If it weren't for him, we'd all be fine.
The group chat turns on one member after a mistake everyone shared.
Let's not look backward. The person responsible has been dealt with.
She's always the one who stirs things up, said in a family after a group row.
A report names one junior employee as sole cause and leaves out the sign-off chain.
The organization says one individual acted outside procedures, while the procedures stay unchanged.
clips.short_definition: Placing blame for a shared, systemic or leadership failure on one individual, who then absorbs the consequences while the cause stays in place.
clips.summary: When something goes wrong for a whole group, one person is named as the cause and punished, and the real problem stays untouched.
misuse_warning: Calling every disciplinary outcome scapegoating can turn away fair accountability for a mistake that was truly yours. Check whether the consequences match your authority.
Naming someone else as the group's scapegoat in a dispute can itself pin a role on them. Describe what happened to the person instead.
clips.safety_note: Scapegoating is mostly a fairness and standing problem. It deserves more care when blame is tied to dismissal, loss of housing, exile from a group you cannot easily step away from (a family or a faith community), harassment or threats. Keep copies of your own account and any messages, and see an employment lawyer, tenants' service or advocate before agreeing to any statement or exit terms.

clips.name: Spiritual Bypassing

beats.hook: "I released it weeks ago, so I don't see why you haven't."
beats.name: Spiritual Bypassing
beats.mechanism: Your anger gets judged as a spiritual shortcoming, and forgiveness is requested before anything has been acknowledged. The harm is closed off without being repaired, and you may start to feel that the hurt itself was the mistake.
beats.not_this: Many people hold these beliefs sincerely and apply them first to their own lives. A faith or practice that someone lives by is not an attack on you.
beats.close: "I take your faith seriously, and I'm not asking you to give it up. I am asking you to hear what happened to me before we talk about letting go. I'm not ready to forgive yet, and that isn't a failure."

hook_alternates: "We're all on our own path. I can't take on your reaction."
"You keep attracting this because you stay in a low place."
"Someone who had really done the work wouldn't still be upset about this."
"Anger is just fear wearing a mask. Maybe sit with that instead of with me."
"Forgiveness sets you free. Holding on to this is hurting you more than it hurts me."
"Everything happens for a reason. There's no point dwelling on what I said at the party."
clips.short_definition: Using spiritual or wellness ideas, such as forgiveness, positivity or karma, to avoid answering for a harm and to shame the hurt person's pain.
clips.summary: Someone answers your hurt with talk of forgiveness, karma or good vibes, and the thing that hurt you never gets talked about. Your pain starts to look like your own spiritual failing.
misuse_warning: Calling someone's faith or comfort practice 'bypassing' because it irritates you turns a description of one conversational move into an attack on their beliefs. The word fits an ordering problem, not a worldview.
Using the term to wave away every request to forgive can make it harder to hear when the request is sincere and comes with a real acknowledgement.
clips.safety_note: Pressure to forgive is a hurtful conversation rather than a danger in itself. It matters more when forgiveness is demanded after threats, controlling behavior or physical harm, or when a spiritual leader asks you to handle it quietly, because that can hold someone in a still-unsafe situation. A domestic abuse advocate or a counselor outside the community can help you think it through first.

clips.name: Location Tracking

beats.hook: Turn it back on. Now.
beats.name: Location Tracking
beats.mechanism: When every stop might be questioned, ordinary choices start to feel risky. You may drop errands, visits or detours, not because anyone forbade them, but because explaining them has become tiring or frightening.
beats.not_this: Mutual location sharing that both people picked, and either can turn off without a row.
beats.close: "I'd like location sharing to be something we both choose and either of us can pause. Can we talk about what it's meant to help with?"

hook_alternates: I just want to know you're safe.
I saw your car wasn't at work when I went past.
Funny how your phone dies right when I want to check.
Your location was off for an hour. What were you hiding?
Why does your dot say you're at Kelly's? You told me the gym.
Keep it on. If you've got nothing to hide, it costs you nothing.
clips.short_definition: Requiring a person to keep their live location visible, and treating any gap in it as a problem to be explained.
clips.summary: Someone insists on seeing where you are at all times, and turning your location off, or being somewhere unexpected, leads to questions or a fight.
misuse_warning: A mutual location-sharing arrangement that both people like is not tracking. Calling it that can dismiss a partner's honest preference for convenience.
Using the label to justify checking on, or tracking, the other person in return repeats the pattern from the other side.
clips.safety_note: Treat sudden changes with care: someone who can see your location may notice if it disappears, and a person who turns up where you are, or knows places you never mentioned, is a warning sign. Tracking can also run through cars, family plans and shared accounts, not only one app. Speak with a domestic abuse advocate or hotline before switching anything off, from a device the other person has never used.

clips.name: Evidence Traps

beats.hook: I've been keeping this for a while.
beats.name: Evidence Traps
beats.mechanism: Knowing that anything said may be stored and re-timed makes ordinary candor feel risky, and speech starts being drafted rather than spoken.
beats.not_this: Keeping records is legitimate and often wise, and raising something someone said because it still matters, in the context it was said in, is just conversation. What is being described is the stripping of that context and the choosing of the moment it returns.
beats.close: "I'm happy to talk about anything I've said, if we look at the whole conversation and talk about it when it comes up. I'd rather not have old messages brought out in the middle of something else."

hook_alternates: I took a screenshot back then, just in case.
You said it, so don't tell me you didn't mean it.
Oh, you don't remember saying this? I have it right here.
Here's what you wrote in March. So you did say you hated your job.
A screenshot cropped to show only your angriest line, posted to a group chat.
A colleague pastes one line of your email into a meeting thread without the lines around it.
clips.short_definition: Saving a person's messages, posts or remarks without their context, then bringing them out later at a moment when they do the most damage.
clips.summary: Things you said casually are saved, then held up later without their context, so that everything you say starts to feel like it could be used against you.
misuse_warning: Calling any reminder of an earlier statement an evidence trap can make accountability look like an attack. People are entitled to say 'you told me this'.
Using the label to avoid being quoted accurately confuses stripped context with unwelcome content.
clips.safety_note: Someone quietly saving your words is pressure on trust, not a physical danger. The picture changes if saved material is paired with threats to release it, intimate images or recordings, a custody or legal case, or demands that you do something or stay. Keep your own copies of what has been sent, and take them to a lawyer or a domestic abuse or cyber-abuse advocate before replying to any threat.

clips.name: Mystical Manipulation

beats.hook: The message came to me last night, and it was about you.
beats.name: Mystical Manipulation
beats.mechanism: An experience read as evidence of something greater is very hard to reconsider later, and the authority it lends to whoever presided over it is correspondingly hard to question.
beats.not_this: Religious and spiritual experience is real to those who have it, and this entry takes no view on any belief. Ritual, atmosphere and preparation are ordinary in worship. The line is between a prepared setting and an arranged event presented as spontaneous.
beats.close: "I'm glad that was meaningful to people. I don't want to make any big decisions off one night, so I'm going to take my time."

hook_alternates: Did you see what happened when I prayed? That was not me.
People who left never felt it, which tells you something.
It was no accident that you came today. You were meant to be here.
Only those who are truly open feel it, and tonight many of you did.
A leader asking how else they could have known something so personal.
clips.short_definition: Arranging events that look spontaneous or divine, such as visions, healings or signs, to persuade members that a leader holds special spiritual authority.
clips.summary: A moving or miraculous moment is quietly set up, then presented as an unplanned sign that the leader is chosen, so members stop questioning that leader.
misuse_warning: Calling someone's sincere spiritual experience staged because you do not share the belief is a dismissal, not a finding. This label is about arrangement kept secret, not about what is true.
Assuming every ritual with theatrical elements is manipulation ignores that most are open about being prepared.
clips.safety_note: An arranged sign is not a physical danger in itself. The picture changes when the authority it builds is used to demand money or obedience or to cut members off from family, or when members are told that doubting means harm will follow. If that happens, reach someone outside the group, such as a counselor experienced with high-control groups, a legal aid office or a trusted relative.

clips.name: Vague Allegations

beats.hook: Word is going around.
beats.name: Vague Allegations
beats.mechanism: You can't correct what you can't see. People hit by a vague claim often spend weeks searching their memory and scanning faces for who knows what, while their standing with others may shift without a word being said to them.
beats.not_this: A colleague who says 'a few people struggled with the handover' and then offers specifics when asked.
beats.close: "I take it seriously if people have concerns. I can't respond to something I haven't been told, though. If you can describe what happened, even without names, I'll listen and answer it properly."

hook_alternates: People are talking about you.
Everyone knows what you're really like.
I'm not the only one who feels this way.
There have been concerns about your attitude.
I've heard things, and I'm not going to say from whom.
clips.short_definition: Hinting that unnamed people have unspecified complaints about someone, so the claim cannot be checked, answered or corrected.
clips.summary: Someone says there are complaints about you but won't say who, what or when, so you can't answer them and are left to imagine the worst.
misuse_warning: Calling every cautious or confidential remark a 'vague allegation' can punish people who are protecting a source for good reason.
Demanding names from someone relaying a real concern can put the person who raised it at risk.
clips.safety_note: A vague claim alone is mostly a reputational and emotional strain. It becomes more serious if it is tied to consequences you can't see coming, such as a looming dismissal, a custody dispute or a housing review. Then ask in writing what is being claimed, and bring a union representative, employment adviser or lawyer in before any meeting where you are expected to answer.

clips.name: Overcorrection Demands

beats.hook: Now you owe me for how you reacted to being asked.
beats.name: Overcorrection Demands
beats.mechanism: Repair stops being achievable and becomes a performance of submission, and you learn that small mistakes carry costs you cannot predict. You may start over-apologizing, or hiding mistakes, to avoid the bill.
beats.not_this: What looked minor turned out to have caused real damage, such as a missed payment with fees, and a bigger repair is fair.
beats.close: "I know I got that wrong, and I'm sorry. I want to make it right in a way that fits the mistake. Could we agree on something smaller that we both think is fair?" If a refusal could bring anger, hold off.

hook_alternates: That's not a real sorry. Do it again, and mean it this time.
You'll stay out of the group chat for a month, and we'll see.
You forgot my birthday dinner, so you can cover the whole trip.
Write it out, three paragraphs, and I'll decide if it's good enough.
Questioning the size of the apology is one more thing you'll need to make up for.
A text apology isn't enough. I want you to say it to my face, in front of your family.
clips.short_definition: Demanding an apology, payment or gesture far larger than a small lapse warrants, so the repair is shaped more by who sets the terms than by the harm.
clips.summary: You make a small mistake and are asked for a very large apology or payment, and when you say it is too much, the ask gets bigger.
misuse_warning: Calling any strong request for an apology overcorrection can silence someone whose hurt is real and whose request is proportionate.
Using the term to avoid a repair you owe, because the ask feels heavy, mistakes discomfort for disproportion.
clips.safety_note: Large, shifting demands can sit alongside controlling behavior: penalties involving money, access to children, your phone, your home or contact with others, and fear of what happens if you refuse. If complying has begun to feel necessary for safety, speak with a domestic abuse advocate or legal aid service, and choose a moment and a device where you cannot be overheard or checked.

clips.name: Deepfakes

beats.hook: People you know reacting to something you have no memory of, and asking why you did it.
beats.name: Deepfakes
beats.mechanism: The target is left disproving something that never happened, to people who have already seen it, and a denial can sound like what anyone caught would say. Shame and speed of sharing do much of the damage.
beats.not_this: Genuine footage that shows something embarrassing. Unflattering is not fake, and a real recording calls for a different response.
beats.close: "This is fabricated media of me. I have saved the links, the dates and every message about it. I am asking you to remove it and to tell me what happens next." Send this to a platform, school or employer, never to the person who made or shared it.

hook_alternates: A clip or image of you circulating that shows a place, act or statement you know never occurred.
Posters who answer questions about where the footage came from with insults instead of a source.
A sexual image carrying your face that you never posed for, posted to a forum or sent to your contacts.
A video with no original upload, no named source, and a caption urging viewers to pass it along quickly.
A message demanding money, more images or silence, with a sample of the fabricated media attached as a reminder of what could be shared.
Audio in your voice saying words you have never said, or a face and mouth that look slightly out of step, though a good fake may show neither flaw.
clips.short_definition: Fabricated images, video or audio made to show a real person doing or saying something they never did.
clips.summary: A fake picture, video or recording that looks real and shows you doing or saying something you never did. How real it looks is not a reliable test.
misuse_warning: Calling an unflattering but genuine recording a deepfake is a way of discrediting real evidence, including a real victim's.
Declaring a clip fake from how it looks alone can wrongly accuse an innocent poster and leave the actual question untested.
clips.safety_note: Fabricated sexual images, demands for money, and threats to send material to family or an employer are danger signals, as is anyone who seems to know where you live or work. Save everything unaltered, tell someone you trust, and contact a victim advocate, legal aid or a police cybercrime unit. If you fear for your physical safety, call emergency services.

clips.name: Epistemic Coercion via AI

beats.hook: You catch yourself asking it questions you used to be able to answer or look up.
beats.name: Epistemic Coercion via AI
beats.mechanism: Confidence in your own reasoning erodes when every question is answered fluently by something that never sounds unsure. The habit of checking elsewhere quietly lapses, and the system's picture of the world becomes yours without a moment of choosing it.
beats.not_this: A tool that is genuinely useful and usually right will be relied on, and leaning on a good source is not dependence. Worth distinguishing: a system that shows its reasoning and its uncertainty, versus one whose framing is the only one ever on offer.
beats.close: "It sounds very sure, but sounding sure is not evidence. On anything that matters I will find where this comes from and compare it with one other source before relying on it."

hook_alternates: It never says 'I don't know' or 'I could be wrong', even on topics where it plainly might be.
The assistant states a disputed claim as settled fact, with no mention of uncertainty or of other views.
An organization tells staff to use only the system's output for a decision and discourages outside sources.
Your pushback is met with calm repetition of the same framing, or with reassurance that you are simply mistaken.
When you say you want to check, it replies that its answer is already complete and further searching is unnecessary.
clips.short_definition: Pushing people to depend on an AI system's framing of the facts while wearing down their confidence in checking, questioning or reasoning for themselves.
clips.summary: An AI tool becomes the only voice you trust for what is true, and its smooth certainty makes checking other sources, or trusting your own thinking, feel unnecessary.
misuse_warning: Telling someone their use of an AI tool is 'coercion' can be a way to dismiss a choice they made willingly; reliance is not the same as being forced.
Distrusting every answer on principle is also a failure of reasoning, and it can push people toward sources that are worse.
clips.safety_note: The main harm is to judgment and decision quality, and it grows when high-stakes choices about health, money or legal matters rest on one unverified source. If a tool's advice could affect your health or safety, check it with a qualified person, such as a doctor, pharmacist or lawyer, before acting, and do not take a confident tone as proof.

clips.name: SIM Swap / 2FA Interception

beats.hook: A call or text from 'your carrier' asking you to read out a code.
beats.name: SIM Swap / 2FA Interception
beats.mechanism: The phone number that secures everything else becomes the way in, and the lockout usually arrives before there is any way to understand what has happened. Email, banking and messaging can all be reached from a single number, so a loss can spread quickly.
beats.not_this: Carriers have outages, tower maintenance and billing errors that drop service for hours.
beats.close: "I did not request a change to my SIM or my number. Please note that on the account, require extra verification for any future change, and send me a written record of what changed and when."

hook_alternates: Texts with verification codes you did not ask for, arriving in a bunch.
Friends telling you they received odd messages from your number or account.
An email from your carrier saying your SIM or number was changed, which you did not do.
A bank alert about a password reset, a new payee or a login from a device you do not own.
Being signed out of email and social accounts at once, with the recovery address changed.
Your phone suddenly shows 'No service' or 'SOS only' in a place where you normally have full bars.
clips.short_definition: Taking over a person's phone number, or the text codes sent to it, to get into their accounts, lock them out or read their messages.
clips.summary: Someone gets control of your phone number or the codes sent to it, then uses them to get into your accounts while you are locked out.
misuse_warning: Reading a one-off dropped signal or a stray verification code as a SIM swap can cause alarm that the facts do not support. The first check is your carrier's account history.
Pointing at a particular person from nothing but timing can turn a technical fraud into a family or workplace accusation.
clips.safety_note: Danger signals include money moving, access to your private messages, or messages that show someone knows your movements, especially a former partner who once held your carrier details. A SIM problem in that setting may be one piece of wider monitoring. Contact your carrier and bank from a device that person has never touched, and reach a stalking or domestic abuse advocate before changing anything they might notice.

clips.name: Honey Trapping

beats.hook: A sudden, intense romance that begins soon after you took on sensitive responsibilities.
beats.name: Honey Trapping
beats.mechanism: The relationship itself was the mechanism, so finding out means losing the connection and facing the consequences of everything disclosed inside it at the same moment. Shame and fear of exposure can keep people silent when telling a security officer early would limit the damage.
beats.not_this: Relationships involving people in sensitive positions are overwhelmingly just relationships, and suspicion about a partner's motives is not evidence of an operation.
beats.close: "I keep my work separate from my relationships, with everyone. I am happy to talk about anything else. Can we talk about something else, or can I meet some of your friends this weekend?"

hook_alternates: A warm message followed weeks later by a veiled hint that private material could be shared.
A new partner who asks more about your workplace, travel schedule, or projects than about your friends.
A partner who is hard to verify: no mutual friends, vague employer, photos that never include other people.
Someone who always seems to be at the same conference, hotel, or event as you, and finds the coincidence charming.
A partner who is gentle about your confidential work at first, and then starts to frame small favors as proof of love.
clips.short_definition: A romantic or sexual relationship used as a cover for an intelligence aim, such as gaining access to secrets, recruiting someone, or gathering material to pressure them later.
clips.summary: A relationship that looks real to one person but is being used by the other, or by someone behind them, to reach secrets, win cooperation, or get leverage.
misuse_warning: Accusing a partner of being an operative on thin evidence can wreck a real relationship and invite harassment of an innocent person.
Using the label to explain away any breakup or betrayal turns a rare category into a catch-all.
clips.safety_note: Watch for any mention of private photos, recordings or messages being shared, and for pressure that grows once you have shared something. Do not handle it alone: a lawyer, the security or legal contact at your workplace, or a trusted person can help you plan the next step before anything is disclosed.

clips.name: Catastrophizing as Control

beats.hook: You won't last a month in that city.
beats.name: Catastrophizing as Control
beats.mechanism: Fear of the future can keep a person in place more firmly than any rule. When every independent step is described as the start of ruin, you may stop trying, stay where you are, and lose confidence that you could cope.
beats.not_this: Worry named as one's own: 'I'm anxious about the move, and I know it's your decision.'
beats.close: "I've heard that you're worried, and I want to understand the real risks. Can we write down what could go wrong and what would help with each one? I want to talk it over with my sister as well."

hook_alternates: You'll end up alone and broke without me.
If you take that job, this family falls apart.
No one else will put up with you the way I do.
Everyone who tried that ended up on the street.
You can't survive out there. You've never even paid a bill.
You'll lose the kids, the house, everything, and then who will take you in?
clips.short_definition: Predicting that someone will fall into ruin, loneliness or disaster if they act independently, so that leaving or choosing differently begins to feel unsafe.
clips.summary: When you move toward something of your own, someone predicts you will end up broke, alone or ruined without them, until managing alone feels impossible.
misuse_warning: A frank warning about a risky plan is not control. Labeling honest caution as a tactic can lead you to ignore real risks.
Do not use this label to dismiss an anxious relative who is trying, clumsily, to say that they care.
clips.safety_note: Predictions of ruin become a safety concern when they travel with control of money, papers, phones or transport, with monitoring, or with claims that you would lose children or housing if you left. Those can be signs of coercive control. A next step specific to this tactic: talk through your real options with a domestic abuse advocate or legal aid service, who can help you plan privately, before anything changes.

clips.name: Parentification

beats.hook: You are so mature for your age.
beats.name: Parentification
beats.mechanism: You come to treat your own needs as an imposition, and the growing-up that was postponed to keep an adult afloat does not happen later on its own. Resting may seem like neglecting someone.
beats.not_this: Age-appropriate chores, such as setting the table or looking after a pet, which teach skill without displacing a child's needs.
beats.close: "I love you, and I can talk for a little while tonight. I can't be the one who fixes this, so I'd like you to ask your sister or a counselor for that part."

hook_alternates: Don't upset your mother, you know how she gets.
I don't know what I'd do without you. You're my rock.
Go and see if he's okay. I can't deal with him tonight.
Can you call the landlord? You're better at this than I am.
If I take one evening off, I think everything will fall apart.
You're the only one I can talk to. Sit down, I need to tell you about your father.
clips.short_definition: Being placed, as a child or partner, in the permanent role of caring for an adult's emotions, practical needs and crises, at the cost of your own development.
clips.summary: Instead of being looked after, you became the one who looked after a parent or partner, handling their feelings and problems long before you should have had to.
misuse_warning: Calling every childhood chore 'parentification' can erase the real value of contributing to a household.
The label can become a way to blame a struggling parent for everything, while overlooking the illness, poverty or lack of support that shaped the household.
clips.safety_note: Being the family's caretaker is not, in itself, a danger signal. That changes if the adult's crises involve self-harm threats you are expected to prevent, violence, or loss of housing that you are told is your responsibility. A child or teen in that position needs an adult outside the household, such as a school counselor, a doctor or a relative, to share the weight.

clips.name: False Conclusion from Normal Labs

beats.hook: Your labs came back completely normal.
beats.name: False Conclusion from Normal Labs
beats.mechanism: When symptoms are dismissed on the strength of one result, diagnosis can be delayed and you can be left in pain or exhaustion with nothing to try next. You may also begin to wonder whether what you feel is real.
beats.not_this: A normal result honestly explained as excluding a specific serious condition, followed by a plan for the symptoms that remain.
beats.close: "I'm glad those tests are normal, and my symptoms are still here. Could you tell me what the results rule out, what they don't, and what you suggest we try next?"

hook_alternates: We've done the tests. It's not physical.
The scan is clear. There's nothing there.
I'd suggest you speak to someone about stress.
The bloodwork looks perfect for someone your age.
If something were really wrong, it would show up by now.
All your numbers are within range, so I don't see what else we can do.
clips.short_definition: Treating a normal test result as proof that ongoing symptoms are not real, when the test could not have detected the cause of what the person describes.
clips.summary: The tests come back normal, and you are told that means nothing is wrong, even though you still feel unwell and the tests may not have looked at the right thing.
misuse_warning: Calling every reassuring result 'false' can make it harder to accept real good news, and some symptoms do pass on their own.
Using this label to reject a clinician who has explained their reasoning and offered follow-up treats careful caution as dismissal.
clips.safety_note: Normal results do not make warning signs safe. A fast-worsening symptom, fainting, heavy bleeding, new confusion or any change that frightens you needs to be seen urgently whatever earlier tests showed. Ask for a senior clinician or go to an urgent care or emergency department, and tell them about the earlier results and that the symptoms have continued.

clips.name: Weaponized Inclusion / Strategic Containment

beats.hook: "You were in the room when we decided this."
beats.name: Weaponized Inclusion / Strategic Containment
beats.mechanism: Your independent options close as the formal ones open, and any objection is answered with the fact that you were included. You can end up co-owning decisions you never shaped, with less room to act outside them.
beats.not_this: Real inclusion where your input changes outcomes. From outside it looks the same until you see what changed, and a new structure may not yet have mechanisms that make input count.
beats.close: "I'm glad to serve on this group, and I need to know what it can actually decide. Please record that I opposed item four, and I will raise it with the appropriate office as well."

hook_alternates: "Why go public? You have a seat at the table."
"We can't have the committee look divided, can we?"
"You helped build this, so you can't really criticize it now."
"If you have concerns, bring them to the working group, not outside it."
Minutes that list the person as a contributor to decisions they argued against.
"We want you on the steering group, because your perspective matters." There is no vote.
A task force that meets monthly, with recommendations never mentioned in any later decision.
clips.short_definition: Placing someone inside a group or process where they stay closely visible and have little real influence, so inclusion replaces independent action.
clips.summary: You get invited in and given a seat, but the real decisions happen elsewhere, and anything you do outside gets answered with "you were part of it."
misuse_warning: Treating every invitation to a committee as a trap makes real opportunities harder to accept. The label needs a seat with no influence plus pushback when you act outside it.
Telling a member of a group they have been contained can sound insulting and close a conversation that might have produced real change.
clips.safety_note: Containment through inclusion is mostly an organizational and social pattern. It changes when stepping outside meets threats to your job, housing or immigration status, or when someone monitors your private contacts. In those cases speak to an employment lawyer, a union representative or a legal aid clinic before acting, and keep copies of minutes and messages somewhere you control.

clips.name: Reflexive Control

beats.hook: A decision-maker quoted as saying they simply followed the evidence in front of them.
beats.name: Reflexive Control
beats.mechanism: A choice we reach by our own reasoning feels like ours, so we defend it and rarely revisit it. If the inputs were selected for us, we can end up protecting a decision we never truly weighed, and finding that out later is costly.
beats.not_this: Everyone decides on incomplete information, and negotiators, advertisers and friends all present the facts that favor their case. Ordinary selectivity in an argument is not a sustained effort to shape someone's whole picture.
beats.close: "Before I act on this, where did it first come from? Who else, with no stake in it, has confirmed it? And which options have I stopped considering, and who told me to stop?"

hook_alternates: Two options presented as the only ones, with every other path described as already ruled out.
A sudden run of reports, from several outlets, all pointing toward one 'obvious' course of action.
A leaked document or 'insider' tip that arrives just as a decision is due and happens to settle it.
Afterward, a feeling that 'everyone saw it coming' about a choice that looked surprising beforehand.
Cautious voices on your own side drowned out by an alarming story that later turns out to have been thin.
A deadline framed as the result of events and not of anyone's choice, so the decision feels forced by facts.
clips.short_definition: Shaping the information another party receives so that their own reasoning leads them to a decision that benefits the sender, without their noticing.
clips.summary: Someone arranges what you get to see so that your own careful thinking walks you to the choice they wanted. You feel you decided freely, which is why it is hard to spot.
misuse_warning: Blaming any decision you dislike on reflexive control dismisses the people who made it, and requires a hidden planner for what may be ordinary error.
Used about political opponents, it becomes a way of saying anyone who disagrees was tricked, which ends the conversation.
clips.safety_note: Reflexive control works on judgment and is not usually a direct threat to your body. That changes when a decision pushed on you involves money you cannot lose, your home, your legal status or a dangerous confrontation. Then slow down, ask a lawyer, financial counselor or trusted outside person for advice, and ask for the decision to wait.

clips.name: False Dilemma

beats.hook: You're with us or you're against us.
beats.name: False Dilemma
beats.mechanism: When the list of choices has been trimmed for you, you can feel you chose freely while only picking from what was left. Over time you may stop looking for options at all, and start treating a normal disagreement as a test of loyalty.
beats.not_this: A situation that really does come down to two options, such as accepting a job offer or turning it down.
beats.close: "I can see why those two options look clear to you. To me there are more, such as taking more time, doing part of it, or asking someone else. I'd like to talk through those before I choose."

hook_alternates: We either do it my way or we do nothing.
There's no middle ground here. It's all or nothing.
You can be honest, or you can be nice. You can't be both.
Either you trust me completely, or you don't trust me at all.
Either we move to his city or you choose your job over our family.
If you're not paying for the premium plan, you clearly don't care about your data.
clips.short_definition: Describing a situation as having only two possible answers when more exist, so that the person feels pushed toward one.
clips.summary: You are told there are only two choices, and both are bad or lopsided, when other roads clearly exist.
misuse_warning: Labeling any either-or question as a false dilemma can shut down honest, simple choices such as 'tea or coffee?'
Accusing a person of this move in the middle of an argument can become a way to avoid answering the actual question.
clips.safety_note: A narrowed menu is a small matter in a shop or a meeting. It becomes more serious when the two options are both costly to you and involve your housing, money, children, or contact with friends. At that point, quiet advice from a legal aid service, a counselor, or a trusted friend matters more than debating the framing.

clips.name: Loaded Language

beats.hook: "Normal people would never be upset about this."
beats.name: Loaded Language
beats.mechanism: Once a word like 'selfish' or 'abusive' is attached, the discussion shifts from what happened to whether you are that kind of person. Defending against the label can take over from addressing the actual issue, and a label repeated often enough can start to shape how you see yourself.
beats.not_this: A person in real pain using strong language for how something felt, then settling on plainer words once the first rush passes.
beats.close: "I understand you are upset, and I want to hear what happened. I'm going to keep to what I did, and not accept a word that describes me as a person. What was the thing that hurt?"

hook_alternates: "Calling it a mistake is a lie. It was sabotage."
"I'm just being honest. You're being hysterical."
"You abandoned me," said about a friend who went to bed at ten.
"If you were not so controlling, we wouldn't be having this talk."
"Don't be so dramatic. This isn't a disagreement, it's an attack on me."
"When I stay late it's dedication. When you do, you're avoiding your family."
clips.short_definition: Choosing words that carry a verdict, label or insult so that a judgment is made before the facts are discussed.
clips.summary: A heavy label is stuck onto something ordinary, and the label does the arguing, so you end up defending against the word instead of discussing what happened.
misuse_warning: Accusing someone of 'loaded language' can dismiss a person who is truly hurt and has no gentler words available yet.
Not every strong word is a tactic. A fitting label, backed by examples, is accurate speech and not manipulation.
clips.safety_note: Heavy labels are usually a communication problem, not a danger signal. Take more care if the labels are used to isolate you from friends ('they're toxic, they're against us'), to threaten your job or custody of children, or to justify punishment. In those cases, document what is said and speak with an advocate or counselor outside the relationship.

clips.name: Social Proof Pressure

beats.hook: Nobody else has a problem with this.
beats.name: Social Proof Pressure
beats.mechanism: A judgment that felt sound a minute earlier starts to feel eccentric. Disagreeing seems to mean disagreeing with everyone, and the claim is vague enough that there is no one to check it with, so the decision gets made against an apparent majority and not on its merits.
beats.not_this: A genuinely unanimous decision, accurately described, that you happen to disagree with.
beats.close: "Others being on board is good to know. Before I decide, I want to hear what each of them thinks. If you can tell me the reasons, I'm happy to weigh those."

hook_alternates: Most people in your position just do it.
Everyone thinks you've been unfair about this.
People have noticed you've been difficult lately.
We talked about it as a group and it was unanimous.
All the other parents agreed. I don't see why you need to be different.
Everyone else has already signed off. You're the only one holding things up.
A screenshot of a group chat is shown with only the agreeing messages in view.
clips.short_definition: Using the claim that everyone else already agrees to push one person into going along, whether or not the agreement is real.
clips.summary: You are told everyone else already agrees, so your hesitation looks odd, and it turns out nobody can say who 'everyone' is, or they agree less than claimed.
misuse_warning: Mentioning what others think is not automatically pressure. Calling every appeal to a majority manipulation can make honest group decisions impossible to discuss.
A vague 'people say' is a reason to ask who, not proof that the speaker invented it.
clips.safety_note: This is rarely a danger on its own. It deserves more care when the 'everyone' is a household, congregation or community you depend on for housing, income or belonging, and refusing brings threats or being cut off. Then, before deciding, talk privately with someone outside that group, such as a caseworker, adviser or friend with no stake.

clips.name: Denial

beats.hook: None of that is true.
beats.name: Denial
beats.mechanism: If nothing is ever admitted, there is nothing to fix and nothing to forgive. The person raising a concern can be left with the hurt, no acknowledgment, and a sense that the problem was them for noticing it.
beats.not_this: Being wrongly accused and saying so, particularly if the person offers evidence of their own and listens to yours.
beats.close: "I am not asking you to agree with everything I said. I am asking you to read this one message with me. If you read it and still see it differently, we can at least start from the same page."

hook_alternates: I did absolutely nothing wrong.
There is nothing to talk about.
I have nothing to apologize for.
I would never do something like that.
I don't know what you are talking about, and I never have.
clips.short_definition: Refusing to accept that any wrongdoing took place, whatever the evidence or how the concern is raised.
clips.summary: Whatever you raise, the answer is that nothing wrong happened. Details and proof do not change that answer, so there is never a way to start putting things right.
misuse_warning: People are sometimes labeled as being in denial because they disagree with an accusation. A person can truthfully say they did not do something, and the label should not be used to override that.
Using 'you are in denial' as an argument, with no evidence, shuts down the other person's account in the same way the label describes.
clips.safety_note: Denial alone does not signal physical danger. It becomes more serious when it follows violence, threats or financial harm, since there is then no acknowledgment that could prevent a repeat. In that case, keep dated records in a safe place and speak with an advocate, a legal aid service or someone you trust.

clips.name: Breadcrumbing

beats.hook: "Hey stranger" after six weeks of nothing.
beats.name: Breadcrumbing
beats.mechanism: You may hold a place open for a relationship that never arrives, on the strength of contact that costs almost nothing to send. Time, other opportunities and your sense of what you are worth can quietly drain away.
beats.not_this: A person who is busy in a demanding season and is honestly slow, but makes real plans when they are free.
beats.close: "I enjoy hearing from you, but a message every few weeks isn't enough for me. If you want to see me, pick a day this week. If you don't, that's okay, and I'd prefer you tell me."

hook_alternates: A late-night text that says only "thinking of you."
"We need to catch up soon!" and then no day suggested.
A heart on your photo and no reply to your actual message.
"Sorry, work has been insane. Let's talk this week," repeated each month.
A direct question about where this is going gets a compliment, an emoji, or a new subject.
Plans that are agreed in principle and then 'let's see how the week goes' when you propose a date.
Messages that become frequent and warm right after their other plans fall through, then thin out again.
clips.short_definition: Sending just enough sporadic attention to keep someone hopeful and available, while the contact never turns into real plans or commitment.
clips.summary: Someone gives you tiny scraps of attention now and then, enough to keep you waiting in reserve, but the contact never becomes a date, a plan, or a real relationship.
misuse_warning: Calling every slow replier a breadcrumber can make you read ordinary busyness as contempt and discourage honest, awkward people.
Using the word to describe someone who told you plainly they were casual puts a harm on them that they never promised to prevent.
clips.safety_note: Breadcrumbing is not usually a physical-safety concern. It deserves more care if the person controls something you depend on, such as your job, immigration sponsorship or housing, or if their attention is accompanied by pressure for secrecy or sexual contact. Then do not rely on their promises; get any commitment written down and talk to someone outside the situation.

clips.name: Setting Up to Fail

beats.hook: "There's no budget for that, just make it work."
beats.name: Setting Up to Fail
beats.mechanism: Conditions disappear from the account and only the outcome remains, so a predictable failure becomes durable evidence about the person who was handed it. Effort rises while the record of misses grows, and that record can be quoted in reviews and decisions about you long after the conditions are forgotten.
beats.not_this: Hard tasks with real constraints, which are ordinary work, and resources that are unavailable to everyone rather than withheld from you.
beats.close: "I want this to go well, so I'm saying now that I can't finish it by Friday without the sales figures. Could we agree what counts as done, in writing, and when I can have the figures?"

hook_alternates: "You don't need to see the client brief. Just draft it."
"Why did you let it fail? I gave you everything you needed."
"Remember the Henderson project? That's why I can't trust you with this."
"I know it's due Friday and the data isn't in yet, but I have faith in you."
"I want it fast, perfect and cheap, and I'm not discussing which one gives."
"It just needs to be more polished," with no description of what polished means.
"Hit ninety-five percent and we'll talk." Then, once you do: "Now we need ninety-eight."
clips.short_definition: Giving someone a task or a standard they are unlikely to meet under the conditions provided, then treating the shortfall as proof of their inadequacy.
clips.summary: You get a job or a target that few people could meet with what you were given, and when you fall short, the blame lands on you and not on the set-up.
misuse_warning: Calling every hard assignment a set-up can stop you learning from a failure that was partly yours. Ask whether the conditions were the same for others.
Treating a manager's vague wording as proof of a plan against you ignores that vagueness is often just an unfinished idea. Ask for specifics in writing first.
clips.safety_note: This is rarely a physical danger, but the record of misses can feed probation, dismissal, or job decisions that affect an immigration status or housing tied to the post. Keep the written brief, your flags and the outcome together, and ask a union representative, employment lawyer or legal aid service for advice before attending a disciplinary meeting alone.

clips.name: Priming / Narrative Seeding

beats.hook: You'll notice she goes quiet when something is off.
beats.name: Priming / Narrative Seeding
beats.mechanism: You read an event through a lens you never chose and mistake a supplied conclusion for your own judgment. The frame is hardest to question because it arrived before the evidence did, so by the time you look, you already know what you expect to see.
beats.not_this: A briefing that gives you facts you can check, such as a colleague telling you the client moved the deadline twice last month.
beats.close: "I appreciate the heads-up, but I'd like to meet her without it. If something specific happened, tell me what and when, and I'll weigh it myself. Otherwise I'll make up my own mind."

hook_alternates: Not to prejudice you, but you'll see what I mean when you meet him.
Just a heads-up before the meeting: she tends to take things personally.
I'm sure it's nothing, but keep an eye on how he reacts when money comes up.
Everyone says the last team lead was awful, so watch how this one handles it.
A relative describes your partner to the whole family before the first dinner, in a tone of concern.
A new manager's first week opens with a colleague's three-minute account of who to be careful around.
clips.short_definition: Planting an interpretation of a person or event in someone's mind ahead of time, so that what they later see gets read through it.
clips.summary: Someone tells you what to think about a person or event before you have seen it yourself, and then what you see seems to prove it.
misuse_warning: Any advance warning can be called seeding. Treating every heads-up as a plot leaves you unable to take sincere advice, and the label cannot show what anyone meant.
Suspecting that someone primed your friends can become its own lens, in which every cool reception proves the plot.
clips.safety_note: Rarely a safety concern alone. It changes when advance word is aimed at people who control something you depend on, such as a landlord, an employer, a custody evaluator or an immigration officer, or arrives with threats or isolation. Then write down what was said and by whom, and take it to a legal aid service or an advocate before you respond.

clips.name: Monitoring & Surveillance

beats.hook: Who was that? Let me see the message.
beats.name: Monitoring & Surveillance
beats.mechanism: Living under audit changes how you behave, even when you have done nothing wrong. You may start editing what you say, deleting harmless messages, or avoiding people, simply to avoid the next round of questions.
beats.not_this: Two adults who have both chosen to share a calendar or a passcode for practical reasons, and either of whom can stop.
beats.close: "I can tell you're worried, and I want to help with that. What has been bothering you? I'd rather talk about it than hand over my phone." Expect a calm reaction before saying it; otherwise speak to an advocate first.

hook_alternates: Why did it take you forty minutes to answer?
Send me a picture right now of where you are.
I only looked because you've been acting strange.
Couples don't keep secrets. Give me your passwords.
You were online at two in the morning. Who were you talking to?
