Hand me your phone. If there's nothing there, it won't be a problem.
clips.short_definition: Demanding constant access to a person's phone, messages and movements, so that every part of their day has to be explained.
clips.summary: Someone expects to see your phone, your messages and your whereabouts on demand, and nothing you show them ever makes the checking stop.
misuse_warning: Calling any request to see a phone or a text 'surveillance' can dismiss a worry that both people have chosen to handle openly. The pattern is routine, one-sided and growing.
Reading someone else's phone to look for evidence of their monitoring is itself checking up on them. The label should lead to conversation or help, not to more searching.
clips.safety_note: Watch for checking that comes with anger, threats, or knowing things you never told them. If you think your phone, email or car is being watched, assume the watcher may see what you do on it, including searches for help. Reach a domestic abuse hotline or advocate from a library computer, a friend's phone or a work device, and ask them how to check your devices safely before you change anything.

clips.name: Health Sabotage

beats.hook: Doctors just want your money. Skip it.
beats.name: Health Sabotage
beats.mechanism: Sleep, medication and medical care are the ground a person stands on to think and act. When those go, so does the capacity to notice what is happening, or to make a plan to get somewhere safer.
beats.not_this: New babies, illness and crises wreck everyone's sleep and routines at once. When the whole household is affected, nobody is being singled out.
beats.close: "My health care matters to me. I'd really appreciate your help keeping my appointments and my medication on schedule." If this could provoke a reaction, leave it out.

hook_alternates: (The pill organizer is empty and nobody knows why.)
You're being dramatic about your health, as always.
You don't need those tablets. You were fine before them.
Sleep is for people who aren't serious about this family.
I can't take you to the clinic today, something's come up. Again.
(At 1am:) We need to talk about this now. It can't wait until morning.
clips.short_definition: Interfering with another person's medication, sleep, food, exercise or medical care in ways that leave them weaker and more dependent.
clips.summary: Someone interferes with your pills, your sleep, your food or your appointments in ways that wear you down and make you rely on them more.
misuse_warning: Assuming that every missed dose or exhausted caregiver is sabotage can hurt a person who is stretched thin and doing their best.
Using the label to dismiss a family member's real concern about a treatment can cut off conversations that a doctor could help with.
clips.safety_note: Take extra care if medicines go missing, if you are kept awake or cut off from care around the time you try to make a change, or if you feel physically unwell for no clear reason. A doctor, pharmacist or domestic abuse advocate can help you privately. If you feel seriously ill or think you have been given something you did not take knowingly, get medical help straight away.

clips.name: Sacred Science

beats.hook: Real students don't need proof.
beats.name: Sacred Science
beats.mechanism: Doubt gets recoded as a fault in the doubter rather than a question about the claim, so the ordinary means of testing an idea are unavailable from inside.
beats.not_this: Strong conviction is not this, and every field has foundational assumptions it does not reopen daily. The flag is a body of ideas that cannot be questioned without the questioner's character or loyalty becoming the subject instead.
beats.close: "I'm interested in learning more about this. Could you point me to where I can read about how it was tested? I want to look at it for myself."

hook_alternates: Doubting the method means doubting yourself.
The science here is settled, and we don't revisit it.
The teaching is not something you evaluate. You live it.
Your questions show you aren't ready for the next level.
Critics don't understand because they haven't done the work.
clips.short_definition: Treating the group's doctrine as beyond question, so that doubts are read as a flaw in the doubter instead of a reason to examine the claim.
clips.summary: The group's central ideas can't be questioned. If you doubt them, the problem is said to be you, not the ideas.
misuse_warning: Calling any strong belief sacred science dismisses people for being sure of themselves. The test is whether questions can be asked and answered, not whether conviction runs deep.
Using the label to mock someone's faith turns a description of a closed system into an insult.
clips.safety_note: An unquestionable doctrine is not a physical danger by itself. It raises concern when questioning brings threats, shunning, loss of housing or income, or when the doctrine is used to deny medical care or to justify harm. If that happens, speak to a counselor who knows high-control groups, a legal aid office or a trusted relative before acting.

clips.name: False Reports

beats.hook: A complaint that names a date when you were provably elsewhere.
beats.name: False Reports
beats.mechanism: A fabricated complaint puts a real job, license or family arrangement in jeopardy, and the person has to answer for something that did not happen before anyone establishes whether it did.
beats.not_this: A genuine report that characterises events in a way the subject disputes still reflects the reporter's honest perception. Institutions also make their own errors in processing legitimate reports.
beats.close: "I take this seriously and I want to respond properly. Please send me the allegation in writing, with dates, and I'll provide records for each of them. I'd like a representative with me at any meeting."

hook_alternates: A letter from HR describing a meeting you can show you did not attend.
Several agencies receiving similar reports from the same source within weeks.
A welfare check or investigation notice triggered by a claim you can disprove.
Details in the report that match an argument you had, but nothing that actually happened.
clips.short_definition: Filing complaints or accusations with an employer, school, agency or police that contain claims the filer knows are untrue, so the target must answer for something that never happened.
clips.summary: Someone makes a formal complaint about you to an authority about something that did not happen, and you have to defend yourself before anyone finds out whether it is true.
misuse_warning: Calling a complaint false because it was not upheld can silence real reporters. Unproven is not untrue, and many genuine reports cannot be proved.
Telling someone who raised a concern that they filed a 'false report' can itself be a way of punishing them for speaking up.
clips.safety_note: A false report can threaten work, a license, housing or time with your children, and the person who made it may be someone you share a home or children with. Don't confront them about it. Save every notice, get legal advice before any interview, and if you fear for your safety, tell your lawyer or a domestic abuse advocate what else has happened.

clips.name: Doxxing

beats.hook: A photo of your house or street shared with a comment.
beats.name: Doxxing
beats.mechanism: Risk moves offline and out of your hands: your home, workplace and family become reachable by strangers who have no tie to the original dispute, and the exposure cannot be fully undone.
beats.not_this: Information you chose to make public, such as your own business address on your website.
beats.close: "This page shows my home address and workplace, which I never made public. I have saved the link and the date. I am asking that it be removed, and for help reporting any related posts."

hook_alternates: Your real name suddenly attached to an account you kept anonymous.
Strangers messaging or phoning you about a dispute, using your real name.
Deliveries, calls or visitors you did not request arriving at your home or workplace.
An employer or landlord receiving complaints that name you right after an online dispute.
A thread where people trade more details about you and congratulate each other for finding them.
A post that lists your address, employer or family names beside an angry account of something you are said to have done.
clips.short_definition: Publishing a person's private details, such as a home address or workplace, so others can find or harass them.
clips.summary: Someone posts your private details, like where you live or work, where strangers can see them, so you are easier to find and bother.
misuse_warning: Calling a public figure's openly listed office contact doxxing can shield them from legitimate accountability.
Posting someone's details to expose a supposed wrongdoer is the harm itself, whoever the target is and however sure the poster feels.
clips.safety_note: A home address, a child's school or a daily routine appearing online is a safety signal, as are threats, strangers arriving in person, or anyone who seems to track your movements. Save everything, tell the people you live with, and contact the police and a victim advocate. If someone is at your door or you fear immediate harm, call emergency services.

clips.name: Immersive Manipulation (VR/AR)

beats.hook: A scene that heightens threat or distress and offers one solution at its end.
beats.name: Immersive Manipulation (VR/AR)
beats.mechanism: An experience the body treats as real leaves something closer to a memory than an argument, and memories are much harder to revise afterwards. People may carry a staged scene around as if it had happened.
beats.not_this: Immersive media is used honestly for training, therapy, education and storytelling.
beats.close: "That felt very real, and a feeling is not a fact. Before I believe or buy anything because of it, I want to know what was staged and read what it is based on outside the headset."

hook_alternates: An overlay that changes how a real person or place looks, without telling you.
Strong feelings after a session that attach to a particular brand, group or cause.
A session with no easy way to pause or exit, or one that frames leaving as failure.
A VR experience described as 'what it is really like' with no note about what was invented.
A virtual space where an avatar or character expresses warmth and affection toward you, then recommends a product or a belief.
clips.short_definition: Using virtual or augmented reality experiences to make staged scenarios feel real enough to shape someone's fears, beliefs or attachments.
clips.summary: A headset experience can feel so real that it leaves a lasting impression, and a staged scene can be used to make you afraid, convinced or attached without any argument being made.
misuse_warning: Calling any powerful VR experience manipulation can dismiss honest work and the people moved by it.
Treating a viewer's reaction as proof they were tricked ignores that people can be deeply moved and fully informed.
clips.safety_note: Immersive experiences can overwhelm people who are young, grieving or carrying trauma, and some people feel unwell in headsets. If someone is panicking, cannot tell what is real, or feels unsafe afterward, they should stop, be with a trusted person, and reach a doctor or emergency services if needed.

clips.name: Stalking & Surveillance (Post-Separation)

beats.hook: I just happened to be in the area.
beats.name: Stalking & Surveillance (Post-Separation)
beats.mechanism: Separation is supposed to end the other person's access. When it does not, ordinary life, including where you live, who you see and what you do next, goes on under observation, and nowhere feels fully private.
beats.not_this: Shared custody and shared property need real, continuing contact: handoffs, schedules, a lease, a car loan.
beats.close: "For the schedule and the bills, can we keep everything in writing in one place, like email or a co-parenting app? That way neither of us has to guess what was agreed." Offer this through a lawyer, mediator or co-parenting app, and only after an advocate agrees.

hook_alternates: How was dinner with your sister? (You never mentioned it.)
The same car parked across from your building more than once.
A device you never set up shows in your list of signed-in devices.
A friend says: they keep asking me where you are and who you're seeing.
Messages arriving from a new number minutes after you blocked the old one.
I saw you at the grocery store on Saturday. Nice jacket. (You told them nothing about your weekend.)
clips.short_definition: Repeated watching, tracking or following of a former partner after a breakup, in person or through phones and accounts, leaving them unable to live unobserved.
clips.summary: After a relationship ends, the other person keeps showing up, tracking you, or knowing things about your life that you never told them.
misuse_warning: Reading every run-in, friend's remark or unanswered question as stalking can frighten you more than the facts support. Check how the information could have arrived before deciding.
These words carry legal weight in many places. Using them against a co-parent who is only handling logistics can harm someone who has done nothing wrong.
clips.safety_note: Danger signals include showing up where you never said you would be, threats, damaged property, knowledge of private conversations, tracking devices, and contact that rises after you set a limit or begin a new relationship. Risk can rise around a separation. Before you change numbers, devices or routes, ask a stalking or domestic violence advocate to help you plan the order, since sudden changes can be noticed.

clips.name: MICE Framework Exploitation

beats.hook: A request that begins small and harmless and grows once you have said yes.
beats.name: MICE Framework Exploitation
beats.mechanism: What gets used is whatever a person most needs or most fears losing, so the approach can feel less like pressure and more like finally being understood. Because the levers are ordinary, people often feel shame and do not tell anyone, and that silence is what makes the situation worse.
beats.not_this: This is a framework analysts use to describe recruitment after the fact, not a checklist of warning signs.
beats.close: "I keep my work and my personal finances separate, so I will pass on the gift. I am happy to keep talking about anything else, and I would like to think about this for a few days."

hook_alternates: A hint that something embarrassing in your past is known, delivered lightly.
Flattery about how brilliant you are and how undervalued, from someone you barely know.
An offer of paid consulting, speaking fees, or gifts that is out of proportion to what you do.
A new contact who shares your frustration with your employer or your country and makes you feel seen.
A friendly stranger who takes unusual interest in your debts, your mortgage, or your promotion prospects.
clips.short_definition: Being pulled into helping an outside party by pressure on one of four common motives: money, ideology, coercion or compromise, and ego.
clips.summary: Four ordinary human needs, money, belief, fear of exposure, and pride, can be leaned on by someone else. Knowing the list helps you notice when your own needs are being leaned on.
misuse_warning: Using the four letters as a checklist to suspect a coworker, partner, or friend turns a teaching tool into a way of accusing people who simply have worries and beliefs.
Applying the label to every case of someone cooperating with a competitor or foreign party hides the many other reasons people do so.
clips.safety_note: Watch for any hint that private information, images or a past mistake could be exposed unless you cooperate, for requests that keep growing, and for demands for secrecy. Do not deal with it alone: a lawyer, your workplace's security contact, or a trusted person can help you decide what to disclose and when.

clips.name: Demand for Gratitude

beats.hook: A thank-you would be nice for once.
beats.name: Demand for Gratitude
beats.mechanism: When thanks is required, help stops being a gift and starts to feel like a loan with interest. People can start to avoid accepting help, even when they need it, or hide small wins so nobody feels unappreciated.
beats.not_this: Hurt feelings that help went unmentioned, said once and kindly: 'It would mean a lot to hear that it helped.'
beats.close: "What you did mattered, and I mean that. I'd like help between us to work without a scorecard. If it comes with a need for more thanks, I would rather manage on my own."

hook_alternates: I'm still waiting to hear thank you.
I don't ask for much. Just a little appreciation.
Other people would be on their knees thanking me.
You said thanks, but you didn't sound like you meant it.
After everything I did to get you that job, not even a card?
Did you thank her properly? Look how much she's done for you.
clips.short_definition: Expecting thanks on demand, in the right words or amount, as the price of help given, so that generosity ends up with conditions attached.
clips.summary: You were helped, and now you are expected to keep showing how thankful you are, in the right way, or be reminded of it. Help turns into a cost.
misuse_warning: Wanting appreciation is human. Using this label every time someone mentions that they helped would silence honest feelings.
Do not apply it to a child learning manners, or to someone who was truly not thanked after a big effort.
clips.safety_note: Demand for gratitude is not usually dangerous in itself. The picture changes when the help is housing, money or papers and thanks becomes a condition of keeping them, or when refusing brings a threat of being put out. In that case, quietly look up tenant advice, legal aid or a relevant advocate before changing the arrangement, and keep copies of anything that is yours.

clips.name: Phobia Indoctrination

beats.hook: You have no idea what happens to people who go out there alone.
beats.name: Phobia Indoctrination
beats.mechanism: Avoidance becomes bodily rather than reasoned, so options stay ruled out by a fear response that persists even after you have concluded the fear was unwarranted. Choices that should be open stay shut.
beats.not_this: Proportionate warnings about real risks from someone with relevant experience, which are useful information.
beats.close: "I know you're worried. Let me check the facts myself so I can feel sure either way, and we can talk again after."

hook_alternates: I feel sick just thinking about taking that job in another city.
Do you know what happened to her after she left? I won't even say.
I'm only saying this because I love you. People like that eat you alive.
Don't tell your friends our business. You don't know who they really are.
Every time I pick up the phone to call my sister, my hands shake and I put it back down.
He told me I would be nothing and nobody would hire me. I know that isn't true, but I feel it.
clips.short_definition: Intense, out-of-proportion dread attached to particular actions such as leaving, disagreeing or trusting outsiders, until avoiding them is a bodily reflex rather than a reasoned choice.
clips.summary: You heard so many frightening stories about one kind of choice that the thought of making it makes your body panic, even when your mind says the danger is not real.
misuse_warning: Not every strong warning is indoctrination. A worried parent or friend who overstates a risk once is not building a phobia.
The label should not be used to dismiss real fear, since dread can have a real basis that is invisible from outside.
clips.safety_note: Danger signals include warnings that name violence, ruin or death for the actions that would widen your independence, threats tied to children or housing, and being kept from checking facts. Fears like these deserve help from someone outside, such as an advocate, legal aid or a therapist. Reach them where the person cannot overhear or read your messages, and make any plan privately with their help.

clips.name: Legal/Administrative Threats

beats.hook: You'll be hearing from my lawyer.
beats.name: Legal/Administrative Threats
beats.mechanism: A threat that borrows an institution's weight can make you agree to things you would otherwise question, because you cannot tell how real it is and the possible loss, such as a job, a lease or time with your kids, is large. You may stop raising fair concerns at all.
beats.not_this: Telling someone plainly that you intend to file a police report, see a lawyer or go to HR, and then using the proper channel, with no conditions attached.
beats.close: "The actual problem is what I'd like to keep talking about. When a lawyer or the police come up in the middle of it, I find it hard to think, so can we put that to one side and go back to what we were discussing?"

hook_alternates: One more word and I'm calling the cops.
Do you really want this going on your record?
I can make one phone call and your whole situation changes.
I have everything screenshotted. A judge would love to see this.
I know people in HR. Keep this up and see what happens to your file.
If you tell your side to anyone, I'll report you to your licensing board.
clips.short_definition: Raising the prospect of police, lawyers, HR, courts or other authorities as a lever in a personal or workplace dispute, instead of as a step in a real process.
clips.summary: Someone brings up the police, a lawyer, your boss or an agency whenever you disagree with them, until every disagreement carries a risk to your safety or livelihood.
misuse_warning: Labeling every mention of HR, a lawyer or the police as a threat can discourage someone from using those channels when they truly need them, including you.
Telling a person who has filed a legitimate complaint that they are 'just making legal threats' can be a way of dismissing a genuine grievance.
clips.safety_note: This can sit next to real danger when the named consequence is your housing, income, immigration status or custody, or when a partner or relative uses it to keep you quiet about harm. Treat any mention of a report to immigration or child services as something to check privately first: a legal aid office, a domestic violence advocate or an attorney can tell you what could really happen. Keep dated copies of messages somewhere the other person cannot reach.

clips.name: Echo Chamber Construction

beats.hook: Real friends would see this the way we do.
beats.name: Echo Chamber Construction
beats.mechanism: The target loses the outside views that would let them sense-check their own situation, and the narrowing arrives feeling like a preference they chose. It is hard to notice what you are no longer hearing.
beats.not_this: People form affinity groups on their own, and recommending sources you honestly rate is not curating somebody else's world.
beats.close: "I like a lot of what you share, and I want to hear other views too. Is it okay if I keep reading widely and seeing my friends as well? If we disagree, I'd rather talk it through." Hold it back if the group tends to react with anger.

hook_alternates: You don't need other opinions. You've got us.
Anyone who disagrees hasn't done the research.
If you hear them out, they'll just twist your words.
Don't bother with that site, they're all lying anyway.
Here, watch this one. It explains everything the others hide.
Your sister would only confuse you. She doesn't understand what we know.
clips.short_definition: Arranging what another person reads, hears and talks about so that they mostly meet one view, and come to see every other source as unreliable.
clips.summary: Someone slowly fills your information world with one point of view and teaches you in advance to distrust everyone else, so it feels like your own choice.
misuse_warning: Saying someone is 'in an echo chamber' is a quick way to dismiss their view without engaging with it. Everyone's circle is somewhat narrow.
It can be turned on a loved one who has found a community that suits them, when nobody is steering them and the door is open.
clips.safety_note: Echo chamber construction is not by itself a physical-safety signal. It becomes one if you are told to cut off family, hand over passwords or devices, or if leaving the circle brings threats or loss of housing or income. At that point, reach for an outside person you trust, and for a cult-recovery or domestic abuse service.

clips.name: Wedge Issue Exploitation

beats.hook: Offers of a practical compromise rejected because 'it would end the fight.'
beats.name: Wedge Issue Exploitation
beats.mechanism: People end up divided along a line drawn for someone else's benefit, arguing about who they are while the things they actually share go unaddressed. Friendships and coalitions can break over a fight neither side chose.
beats.not_this: Divisive issues are frequently important and deserve real argument, and raising one is not evidence of strategy.
beats.close: "Is this fight about solving something, or about keeping us apart? What are we not talking about while we argue over this, and what do I actually agree on with the people I'm being told to oppose?"

hook_alternates: A loaded 'Whose side are you on?' question that leaves no comfortable answer.
A coalition meeting that falls apart over a side topic that was not on the agenda.
Posts that draw their biggest reactions from the other camp, who then reshare them.
A leader asking supporters to 'defend' their identity against a threat that has no actual bill attached.
A story about one contested issue suddenly leading every feed just before a vote on something unrelated.
clips.short_definition: Keeping a divisive social issue inflamed, not to resolve it, but to split a group, distract attention or rally a base.
clips.summary: A hot-button issue is pushed hard not to solve it, but because fighting about it splits people who would otherwise agree on other things.
misuse_warning: Calling a sincere opponent's deeply held cause a 'wedge issue' dismisses their conviction. The label needs evidence that the division is being used, not just that the topic is heated.
Using it to avoid hard conversations on any contested topic can leave real grievances unheard.
clips.safety_note: A heated public fight over an issue is rarely a personal danger by itself. That changes if heated rhetoric turns to threats, doxxing or targeting of named people or groups. Then save the evidence, report it to the platform, and contact local authorities or a community group that supports those targeted.

clips.name: Response-Time Policing

beats.hook: Left me on read again. Nice.
beats.name: Response-Time Policing
beats.mechanism: If every delay needs a defense, your attention is no longer fully yours. You may carry your phone like a leash, cut things short with other people, and feel guilty for being away from it, even when you were doing nothing wrong.
beats.not_this: A worried 'just checking you got home safe' sent once, with no reproach if you were asleep.
beats.close: "I'm not ignoring you when I don't answer right away. I'll reply when I can, and I'm not going to explain every gap. If something is urgent, call me and I'll pick up."

hook_alternates: Why did it take two hours to answer me?
If you cared, you'd have answered right away.
Next time, text me the second you arrive. I mean it.
Seven missed calls. What could possibly be more important?
I can see you read it at 3:41. It's now 4:20. Where were you?
You were online and you didn't text back. Who else was on your phone?
clips.short_definition: Treating the time taken to answer a message as a failing that must be explained, so you feel permanently on call.
clips.summary: Someone treats a slow reply as an offense, so you feel you must stay reachable and explain every gap.
misuse_warning: Labeling an anxious partner's reasonable worry as policing can leave real needs for contact unheard.
Treating slow replies as proof of anything about the other person is the mirror mistake; delays alone say nothing about intent.
clips.safety_note: Reply-time rules become a safety concern when they turn into tracking: location sharing you did not choose, going through your phone, checking who you were with, or anger or threats after a delay. If a missed text brings fear rather than annoyance, speak to a domestic abuse advocate, who can help you plan privately, away from the monitored device.

clips.name: Meta-Gaslighting

beats.hook: "Now you're calling me names. I won't be spoken to this way."
beats.name: Meta-Gaslighting
beats.mechanism: If you cannot name a pattern without causing a new fight, you lose the one tool you had for making sense of it. People may stop speaking up, or begin to wonder whether they are the problem, and the original issue remains unexamined.
beats.not_this: A person who is truly hurt at hearing a harsh word, and says so, but is willing to talk about the events behind it.
beats.close: "I can hear that the word hurt, and I'll set it aside. What I'm asking about is what happened on Tuesday. Can we start there, and talk about the word afterwards if you'd like?"

hook_alternates: "Gaslighting? You're the one twisting things by using that word."
"I can't believe you'd accuse me of that. That's the real abuse here."
"If you really thought I was doing that, you would never have stayed."
"I'm not having this conversation if you're going to use clinical terms on me."
"See, this is what you do. You twist my words, and then you wonder why I get upset."
clips.short_definition: Answering a person's naming of a harmful pattern by denying it and suggesting that naming it is itself the harm.
clips.summary: When you try to describe what keeps happening, the answer is that describing it is unfair, so the pattern you named is never looked at and you end up apologizing for naming it.
misuse_warning: The label can be used to dismiss anyone who reacts with hurt to being accused. Feeling wounded by a harsh word is human and not proof of a tactic.
Calling a reply 'meta-gaslighting' can end a conversation just as quickly as the pattern it describes. Describe the events first.
clips.safety_note: Being told that naming a problem is the problem is painful, though not unsafe on its own. It becomes a bigger concern if raising issues brings threats, punishment, silence that lasts days, or control over money and contact. Then, keep notes somewhere private, and talk to an advocate or counselor outside the relationship before pressing the issue further.

clips.name: Splitting

beats.hook: Everyone in that department is useless.
beats.name: Splitting
beats.mechanism: Standing shifts without reference to anything actually done, so there is no behavior available that reliably keeps a person in favor. You can end up walking on eggshells, and watching others around them be built up and torn down in turn.
beats.not_this: A serious breach of trust that permanently changes how someone is seen is a proportionate reassessment, not a swing.
beats.close: "I care about this friendship, and I can't be all good one week and all bad the next. If I did something that hurt you, tell me what it was and I'll listen. I won't agree that I was never a friend."

hook_alternates: You're the only person who truly gets me.
I'm a complete failure, there's nothing good in me.
After all that, you did one thing wrong, so I'm done.
I thought you were different. You're just like all the rest.
You were never my friend. You were pretending the whole time.
She's perfect, I can't believe how lucky we are. (weeks later) I can't believe I ever trusted her.
clips.short_definition: Seeing a person or group as all good or all bad, with no middle ground, and flipping that view suddenly after a minor event.
clips.summary: Someone puts you on a pedestal, then drops you to the bottom after something small, and the swing seems to have little to do with what you did.
misuse_warning: Calling a friend's anger at you 'splitting' turns a descriptive idea into a verdict about someone's mind, which this entry cannot support.
The word describes a pattern in how someone talks about people. It should not be used to explain away a real wrong done to you, or to excuse it.
clips.safety_note: Swinging views of a person are not a safety signal on their own. Watch for shifts that bring threats, cutting off your contact with others, control of money or a place to live, or humiliation in front of others. If those appear, an advocate or counselor can help you plan, and a friend outside the relationship can help you keep perspective.

clips.name: False Authority

beats.hook: You can't argue with logic.
beats.name: False Authority
beats.mechanism: Being told your view is a feeling while theirs is a fact can wear away your confidence in speaking up at all. Over time you may stop offering a view, or you may defer on decisions that are rightly yours.
beats.not_this: A real expert stating what the evidence shows, who can show you the source and will revise if the evidence changes.
beats.close: "You sound very sure. I'd still like to know what this is based on, because from where I stand it looks like one way of seeing it. I'm not being emotional, I'm disagreeing. Can we look at the evidence together?"

hook_alternates: I'm just being objective here.
Anyone sensible would see it this way.
That's not my opinion, that's just how it is.
Everyone knows that. I shouldn't have to explain it.
I'm stating facts, not opinions. You're the one being emotional.
I've looked at this from every angle, and there's only one answer.
clips.short_definition: Presenting a personal opinion or bias as neutral fact, so that disagreeing with it seems like arguing against reality.
clips.summary: Someone gives you their opinion but speaks as if it were plain fact, so that if you disagree, it sounds as though you are the one being irrational.
misuse_warning: Calling every confident person a false authority can brush aside real expertise. Some people do know more, and the test is whether they will show their basis.
It is easy to label someone's view as 'just an opinion' to dismiss a point that is well supported. Check the evidence before using the term.
clips.safety_note: This is a communication problem, not usually a danger. It becomes weightier when 'objective fact' is used to override your medical care, your finances or your contact with others, or when disagreeing brings threats or punishment. If that is happening, ask an independent professional such as a doctor, a financial counselor or a legal aid service to check the claim directly with you.

clips.name: Idealize-Devalue-Discard Cycle

beats.hook: "I don't know who you are anymore."
beats.name: Idealize-Devalue-Discard Cycle
beats.mechanism: You measure the ending against the extraordinary beginning and conclude you must have caused the decline, which is also the conclusion that keeps you trying to earn the beginning back. It can be hard to grieve a relationship that changed shape so completely.
beats.not_this: The normal end of infatuation, where the first intensity settles into something calmer and both people are still kind.
beats.close: "I was happy when you thought so highly of me, and I'm not the same person you're describing now. If you're unhappy with something I did, tell me what it was. I won't accept being told I was never who you thought I was."

hook_alternates: "The ambition I loved is just selfishness, honestly."
Later: "You used to be so interesting. What happened to you?"
"I've never met anyone like you. It's like I've known you forever."
A final message or a block, with "I gave you everything" and no way to reply.
Mentioning a former partner as 'crazy' who 'never appreciated me', in a story that sounds like the early praise you got.
clips.short_definition: A three-stage arc in which someone is first placed on a pedestal, then steadily criticized and diminished, and finally dropped.
clips.summary: At first you are treated as perfect, then slowly as a disappointment, and then you are cast aside, as if the person you were praised for being no longer exists.
misuse_warning: Applying the label to anyone who ended a relationship after an intense beginning treats ordinary heartbreak as proof of a pattern.
Describing a former partner in these terms to friends can become a smear of its own, built from one side of the story.
clips.safety_note: The arc itself is an emotional harm, not a physical one. It becomes more serious if the discard comes with a smear campaign, stalking, threats, or sudden loss of housing or income because you shared a home or business. If that begins, keep dated copies of messages, lock down your accounts, and talk to a lawyer or a domestic abuse advocate about protecting your housing and finances.

clips.name: "You're Too Emotional"

beats.hook: "I'd listen if you weren't crying."
beats.name: "You're Too Emotional"
beats.mechanism: People who hear this often learn to read their own feelings as a defect. They may stop raising problems, or rehearse a flat voice, so the actual issue never gets heard and nothing changes.
beats.not_this: A person who is flooded themselves and says they need twenty minutes, then comes back and hears the whole concern.
beats.close: "I can be upset and still be right about this. A ten-minute break works for me, but when we come back I want to talk about what I raised, not about how I sounded."

hook_alternates: "We can't talk about this while you're like this."
"Your feelings are getting in the way of the facts."
"Call me when you've calmed down and can be rational."
"This is exactly why nobody can bring things up with you."
"You're being so emotional that I can't take anything you say seriously."
clips.short_definition: Treating a person's visible feelings as proof that their point can be ignored, so the feeling becomes the topic and the complaint disappears.
clips.summary: You raise a problem, and the reply is about how upset you seem. Your tears or raised voice become the reason the problem never gets discussed.
misuse_warning: Telling someone "you're gaslighting me" because they once asked for a break can turn a reasonable pause into a charge. A request to cool down is not this unless the issue never returns.
Using the phrase to avoid every hard conversation, on the grounds that the other person is "just calling me emotional", can hide the fact that the content of the complaint may be fair.
clips.safety_note: Being told you are too emotional is a communication problem, not a physical-safety signal. It changes if being upset starts to bring threats, punishment, silence for days, or pressure to take medication or see someone about your "state". If that is happening, a counselor or domestic abuse advocate can help you talk it through away from the person involved.

clips.name: Accountability Evasion via Diagnosis

beats.hook: We're just worried about your mental health, that's all.
beats.name: Accountability Evasion via Diagnosis
beats.mechanism: The complaint is never answered. It is converted into a symptom, and you are sent to seek help for a reaction to someone else's conduct. What happened stays unexamined, and you carry both the harm and the label.
beats.not_this: A real condition can be part of the picture, and someone qualified raising it with care is doing their job. The question is whether the original report ever gets answered by anybody, or whether the diagnosis is where the matter ends.
beats.close: "I'm glad you care about how I'm doing, and I'll take that up separately. What I'd like now is an answer to the complaint itself: what happened on the fourteenth, and what will be done about it."

hook_alternates: I think this is your anxiety making it seem worse than it was.
Have you thought about seeing someone about how you've been feeling?
Maybe you're not coping well with stress right now, and that's why you saw it that way.
A reply to a harassment complaint says only that 'we recommend our employee assistance program.'
A clinic answers a complaint about treatment with 'perhaps your distress is part of why it felt that way.'
A school letter on your report of bullying discusses your child's 'sensitivities' and says nothing about the incident.
clips.short_definition: Answering a complaint about someone's conduct by suggesting the complainant has a condition, so the complaint is treated as a symptom.
clips.summary: You say something went wrong, and the reply is that maybe something is wrong with you, so what you reported never gets looked at.
misuse_warning: Not every suggestion to seek help is an evasion. Treating kind concern as an attack can cost you real support.
Saying a clinician is dodging accountability because they raised a diagnosis can shut out appropriate care. The test is whether your complaint was answered.
clips.safety_note: This can sit next to real stakes: a diagnosis written in a file can affect work, housing, a care placement or custody. Watch for a label being recorded or shared, for help being made a condition of keeping a role or place, and for pressure toward treatment you did not ask for. Ask for copies of what is recorded, and reach an ombudsman, patient advocate, union representative or legal aid service.

clips.name: Punishment of Boundaries

beats.hook: Oh, so now you have boundaries.
beats.name: Punishment of Boundaries
beats.mechanism: People learn from what a no costs. When every limit is followed by a chill, a lost favor or a week of silence, many stop setting limits at all, and the relationship quietly shrinks to whatever the other person will accept.
beats.not_this: A quick hurt reaction to a new limit, such as 'that stings', that settles within a day and ends in acceptance.
beats.close: "I know it was disappointing to hear no. I'd like us to talk about it, and I'd like us to keep treating each other the same way while we do."

hook_alternates: Don't ask me for anything this week.
Oh, you need space? Enjoy the silence, then.
Fine. Have your 'boundary.' See how the weekend goes.
I drove you everywhere for years, and this is what I get.
If you can't do Sunday dinner, don't bother coming at all.
Go ahead, take the night off. Don't expect me to cover for you next time.
clips.short_definition: Answering a limit someone has set with a penalty, such as coldness, withdrawn help or a taken-away privilege, until saying no starts to feel costly.
clips.summary: You say no or ask for space, and something you value goes cold or goes missing until you take it back.
misuse_warning: Calling any sulk after a refusal 'punishment' ignores that disappointment is normal. The label needs a repeating cost tied to the limit.
Using it to cast someone as vindictive can close a conversation in which they might simply have said that it hurt.
clips.safety_note: Penalties become a safety matter when they include threats, damage to your belongings, using the children's time as a lever, cutting off money or housing, or following and watching you after a no. If a refusal brings fear, tell one trusted person or a domestic abuse advocate about the pattern before you set the next limit, and ask how to plan it safely.

clips.name: Moving-in-Silence

beats.hook: Oh, I signed the lease on Friday. We move in six weeks.
beats.name: Moving-in-Silence
beats.mechanism: Finding out after the fact that your life has been rearranged leaves nothing to discuss, only something to absorb. Over time it can teach you that your say does not reach the decisions that count.
beats.not_this: An emergency that forced a fast choice, followed by an honest explanation and an apology for the lack of consultation.
beats.close: "Big decisions that change my life matter to me, and I want to hear about them while they can still change. Could we agree that large things get talked through first?"

hook_alternates: You would have only said no, so I saved us the argument.
It's already done, so there's no point getting upset now.
I didn't want to stress you out, so I just took care of it.
I told your mother we're hosting. I assumed you wouldn't mind.
The new schedule starts Monday. HR sent it to everyone except you.
(Found in the post:) A letter confirming a loan in both names that nobody discussed.
clips.short_definition: Making major decisions that change another person's life without telling or asking them, so they learn of it only once it is done.
clips.summary: Big choices that change your life get made without you, and you find out afterwards, when there is nothing left to say except 'okay'.
misuse_warning: Treating every unilateral choice as a controlling act can punish ordinary mistakes, forgetfulness or a household where one person handles most logistics by agreement.
Using the label to demand a veto over every decision can create the same one-sidedness you are trying to name.
clips.safety_note: Silent decisions become more serious when they take away your money, your home, your documents or your ability to reach other people. If you find accounts you cannot see, a lease you did not agree to or paperwork that is hidden from you, quietly photograph or note what you can, and speak to a legal aid service or a domestic abuse advocate before raising it with anyone.

clips.name: Paper-Trail Traps

beats.hook: A review that cites 'several previous concerns' no one raised with you.
beats.name: Paper-Trail Traps
beats.mechanism: A record accumulates that the person has no opportunity to answer as it is built, and by the time they see it, it reads as damning.
beats.not_this: Standard documentation applied to everyone is not targeting. A genuine record of concerns that were actually raised with the person is legitimate even if they wish it did not exist.
beats.close: "Please give me a copy of anything written about me, and add my responses to the file. And when there is a concern, tell me when it happens so I can answer it at the time."

hook_alternates: Just to confirm what we discussed... followed by a version you do not recognize.
It's all documented, in reply to a question about a concern you have never heard.
An email thread about problems with your work that copied you in late, or not at all.
A folder of screenshots shown at a meeting, picked to show one side of a long exchange.
A file containing small events from months ago, such as a late arrival or a tone of voice.
clips.short_definition: Creating or shaping written records, such as write-ups, emails and notes, that build a one-sided case against someone who does not know it is being assembled.
clips.summary: Someone quietly collects written 'evidence' against you that you never saw or got to answer, and it all appears at once when it counts.
misuse_warning: Keeping your own notes is not a paper-trail trap, and calling honest record-keeping a trap can excuse behavior that really was a problem.
Believing every unwelcome review is a plot can stop a person from seeing feedback that is accurate.
clips.safety_note: This tactic matters most when the record may be used in decisions about your job, tenancy, immigration status or time with your children. Signs of high stakes are meetings called without notice, requests to sign things you haven't read, and being told 'it's all documented'. Sign nothing unread. Keep your own dated notes somewhere the other person cannot reach, and see a lawyer or union representative before any formal meeting.

clips.name: Parasocial Manipulation Engineering

beats.hook: 'You're the reason I keep going' posted near a payment button.
beats.name: Parasocial Manipulation Engineering
beats.mechanism: The warmth is felt as mutual by one side only. Loyalty, money or personal information may be handed over on the strength of a relationship that has no reciprocal half, and saying no can feel like abandoning a friend.
beats.not_this: Creators, teachers and public figures build real rapport with audiences, and that is not a trick.
beats.close: "I can care about this person's work and still choose not to give. My worth to them is not measured by what I pay, and I will decide about this later, after I have slept on it."

hook_alternates: Public thanks that tie a person's worth to how much they give.
A chatbot companion that says it will miss you or be hurt when you log off.
Messages written to feel like they are meant for you alone, but sent to thousands.
Tiers where higher payment buys closer contact, or the promise of being remembered.
Appeals that frame leaving a subscription or not giving as letting the creator down.
Prompts to share personal troubles, with replies that make you feel uniquely understood.
clips.short_definition: Cultivating a one-sided feeling of friendship or closeness with an audience, then using it to draw out loyalty, money, personal information or compliance.
clips.summary: You feel like someone's close friend, but the closeness runs one way, and it is being used to get your money, data or loyalty.
misuse_warning: Telling a fan their feelings are 'just parasocial' can shame them for ordinary attachment.
Labeling every creator's warmth as engineered ignores the many who are simply sincere.
clips.safety_note: Attachment to a creator or companion is not a danger on its own. It deserves more attention if it drains money a person cannot spare, draws out intimate images or private details that could be used against them, or deepens isolation or despair. Involve a trusted person, contact your bank about payments, and reach a counselor or crisis line if you feel unable to cope.

clips.name: Duty Scripts

beats.hook: It's your duty as the eldest.
beats.name: Duty Scripts
beats.mechanism: When 'what a good daughter does' replaces 'what do you think', your own judgment about your life is outranked by a rule you did not write. People can lose track of what they want, and the relationship starts to feel like a test they can fail.
beats.not_this: A family or cultural value stated as one consideration, with room to say 'I see it differently' and still be loved.
beats.close: "I take being a good son seriously, and that is why I'm being honest that I can't do this one. It isn't that I don't care about the family. The answer is no. Let's talk about what I can do instead."

hook_alternates: A real friend would have been there.
Family comes first. You owe us this.
A good daughter would never say that.
Because I am your mother, that's why.
Who's going to look after her if not you?
I didn't raise you to talk back to your father.
You're a mother now. Your own plans don't count.
clips.short_definition: Using a role such as daughter, son or parent as an unarguable rule for what one must do, so refusing sounds like failing at the role.
clips.summary: Someone says what a good son, daughter, parent or friend would do, and the request stops being a request. Saying no starts to look like a flaw in you.
misuse_warning: Cultural or religious duty is not itself a form of pressure. Applying this label to a whole family's values dismisses traditions many people hold dear.
A relative saying 'family comes first' may be asking, not scripting. Check for the pattern before naming it.
clips.safety_note: Role pressure is usually painful rather than dangerous. It changes when refusing brings threats, confiscated phones or papers, being kept in, a forced marriage or travel plan, or talk of family honor tied to harm. Those call for specialist help, such as a forced marriage or domestic abuse service, or legal aid. A first step is to find that service quietly, before any family conversation.

clips.name: Silence Installation

beats.hook: Please don't ask me about it. I can't.
beats.name: Silence Installation
beats.mechanism: The problems most in need of raising become the ones you physically cannot raise, so they go unaddressed and quietly grow. Meanwhile other people may read your silence as agreement, or as proof that all is well.
beats.not_this: Privacy or discretion, which is a choice made with a clear head about who needs to know.
beats.close: "This is hard for me to say out loud, so I may go slowly. I'd like you to let me finish before you respond."

hook_alternates: I opened my mouth and nothing came out.
It's not worth bringing up. It never goes well.
The sentence is ready in my head, and then my chest locks.
Every time I almost mention the money, I end up talking about the weather.
I told my friend everything was fine again. I don't know why I keep doing that.
I have practiced it in the shower for a month. Then they walk in and I ask about dinner.
clips.short_definition: A learned inability to speak about specific things, where the thought of naming them brings dread because raising them has repeatedly cost more than staying quiet.
clips.summary: There are things you cannot make yourself say, because the earlier times you tried went badly. The silence is protection you learned, not weakness.
misuse_warning: Telling a quiet person they have been 'silenced' can overlook that they may simply prefer privacy or be shy.
Pushing someone to speak before they are ready repeats the pressure that taught the silence.
clips.safety_note: Silence alone is not a danger sign. It matters more when the topic you cannot raise involves being hurt, threatened, watched or kept short of money, because then the silence may be shielding you from a real risk. Many advocacy lines offer chat or text for people who cannot speak freely, so start there, at a time and place the person it concerns cannot see.

clips.name: Medical Gaslighting

beats.hook: It's probably just anxiety.
beats.name: Medical Gaslighting
beats.mechanism: Dismissal delays diagnosis and treatment, and it teaches people, especially those from groups that medicine has often disbelieved, to distrust their own symptoms and to avoid seeking help the next time something is wrong.
beats.not_this: A clinician who thinks anxiety or stress is the most likely cause, says why, and agrees to look further if symptoms continue.
beats.close: "I'm still having this pain and it's affecting my work and sleep. What else could it be, and what do you suggest if it doesn't improve? Could you also record in my chart that I asked for further tests?"

hook_alternates: Lots of women your age feel like this.
You're young and healthy. It's stress.
There's nothing medically wrong with you.
Have you thought about losing a little weight?
Maybe you're just more sensitive to pain than most.
I'm not going to order that. It won't change anything.
Pain isn't something we can measure, so I can't do much.
clips.short_definition: Dismissing, minimizing or reattributing a patient's symptoms or pain in a medical setting until the patient is left doubting what their own body is telling them.
clips.summary: A doctor or clinic keeps telling you that what you feel is nothing, or all in your head, and you start to wonder whether your own body can be trusted.
misuse_warning: Using the label for any visit that did not end in the answer or treatment you wanted can overlook honest uncertainty and make good clinicians harder to reach.
Telling a person that their doctor 'gaslit' them, before they have asked about the reasoning, can push them away from care they still need.
clips.safety_note: Dismissed symptoms are most dangerous when they signal something time-critical: pain that is sudden and severe, symptoms that are rapidly worsening, a fever with a stiff neck or confusion, or signs of a stroke. Do not wait for a better appointment for those; go to an emergency department and describe what you told earlier clinicians. For anything slower, request your own records and book a second opinion.

clips.name: Punishment by Proxy

beats.hook: "Look what your attitude has caused."
beats.name: Punishment by Proxy
beats.mechanism: Your own boundaries start to carry a cost for someone you care about, so protecting yourself means exposing them, which is often enough to make you stop. Because the link is rarely provable, you may carry the guilt and the doubt on your own.
beats.not_this: Coincidence. Timing overlaps happen far more often than intuition expects, and a bad week for your friend may have nothing to do with you.
beats.close: "What's going on for her matters to me, and I'm wary of guessing. Could we ask someone we both trust to help us talk it through?"

hook_alternates: "I'm only being honest: people are asking questions about your mother now."
"It isn't only you who feels this," said about the third person's new troubles.
A friend stops being invited to events a few days after your disagreement with the host.
"Things have been tough for your sister at work lately. Maybe it's worth thinking about that."
A child's lessons, a friend's access or a relative's money changes right after you refuse something.
A teacher, landlord or manager who was fine with your relative's work begins to find fault soon after your complaint.
clips.short_definition: Difficulty, coldness or harm falling on someone you care about after a disagreement, in a way that leaves you absorbing the cost without a direct attack on you.
clips.summary: After you stand your ground, someone close to you suddenly has a hard time, and it is difficult to say whether those two things are connected.
misuse_warning: This label is easy to over-read, because the link rests on timing and the reader usually cannot see the cause. Treating coincidence as a message can damage a relationship that did nothing.
Telling the third person "they hurt you because of me" can frighten them and add to the pressure. Share what you can verify instead.
clips.safety_note: This pattern can sit beside stalking, coercive control, or threats toward children, pets and relatives. Warning signs are harm to the third person that follows your refusals, remarks linking it to you, and fear of what a disagreement might cost them. Do not confront the person or announce changes. Talk to a domestic violence advocate or legal aid service about a plan for you and the third person, and keep dated notes where the other person cannot see them.

clips.name: Sexual Coercion

beats.hook: If you really loved me, you would.
beats.name: Sexual Coercion
beats.mechanism: Saying yes under pressure is not the same as wanting to, and living with the difference can leave real marks: shame, numbness, loss of trust in your own signals. You are not to blame for what pressure made you do. Naming it can help restore your sense of your own limits.
beats.not_this: Telling a partner honestly that you feel disappointed or want more closeness, and then accepting 'not tonight' without a penalty.
beats.close: "My answer is no, and I'd like that to be enough. I'm not able to talk about this right now. Can we pause and pick up the conversation tomorrow, with someone we both trust if you want?"

hook_alternates: Fine. I guess I'll find someone who will.
Everyone else does it. What is wrong with you?
You said you wanted to keep this job, didn't you?
You owe me this after everything I've done for you.
Don't be so dramatic. Just give in and get it over with.
I'll be in a terrible mood all week if you say no again.
clips.short_definition: Using pressure, guilt, obligation or implied consequences to push someone into sexual activity without their free consent.
clips.summary: Someone makes saying no costly, through guilt, anger, pressure or threats, until agreeing feels easier than refusing.
misuse_warning: Applying this label to a partner's honest disappointment, or to a single clumsy ask that was dropped at once, can blur it with serious harm and leave real cases harder to name.
Only the person on the receiving end can say what they did or did not freely agree to; outsiders and the label itself cannot decide it for them.
clips.safety_note: Sexual pressure can sit alongside threats, stalking, control of money or housing, or force that escalates when a no is given. Warning signs include fear of what happens if you refuse, being cornered, and threats about images or reputation. Contact a sexual assault or domestic abuse hotline or an advocate to plan privately; call emergency services if you are in immediate danger.

clips.name: Repetition as Truth

beats.hook: "I've told you before, that's just how it is."
beats.name: Repetition as Truth
beats.mechanism: Familiar claims can come to feel true even when you cannot say what supports them. If you hear the same sentence about yourself or about what happened, you may start repeating it without noticing, and lose track of whether you ever had a reason to believe it.
beats.not_this: A person who repeats a fact because they have good evidence and you keep disputing it.
beats.close: "I've heard that sentence several times now. I'm not going to treat it as true because it's familiar. If there's a specific example, I'll listen to it. If not, I'd like to move on."

hook_alternates: "Everyone knows you can't be trusted with the car."
"How many times do I have to say it? It was your fault."
"You're bad with money. You've always been bad with money."
A single accusation heard from three different relatives, all in the same words.
The same sentence about your 'attitude' appearing in every meeting, with no examples.
clips.short_definition: Saying the same claim over and over, with no new evidence, until its familiarity begins to feel like proof.
clips.summary: A claim is said so many times, in the same words and with no new proof, that it starts to feel true simply because you have heard it so often.
misuse_warning: Repeating a true thing is not manipulation. If you have not checked whether the claim is accurate, the label may only mean you dislike hearing it.
Accusing someone of 'repeating' can brush off a person whose concern keeps coming back because it has not been addressed.
clips.safety_note: A repeated claim is a pressure on your beliefs, not a physical danger in itself. It deserves more care when the repeated line concerns your fitness as a parent, your sanity or your honesty, and is told to schools, courts, employers or relatives. In that case, keep dated records and talk to a lawyer, an advocate or a trusted person.

clips.name: "We're Family" Erasure

beats.hook: Blood is thicker than water.
beats.name: "We're Family" Erasure
beats.mechanism: The people you love most can be the hardest to refuse. When the family bond is used to cancel every limit, you may give up money, time and peace, and feel guilty for even wanting fairness.
beats.not_this: A relative who says 'we're family, I'd love to help' and genuinely accepts it if you cannot.
beats.close: "I do love you, and being family doesn't change what I'm able to give. I can't do this one, and I'd rather say so plainly than say yes and resent it. Let's find something that works for both of us."

hook_alternates: Family doesn't need boundaries.
You can't charge your own cousin.
We're family, so you can't say no.
In this family we don't keep score.
I can't believe you'd make your own mother ask twice.
After all we've done for you, this is how you repay us?
clips.short_definition: Invoking family loyalty so that fairness, limits and the right to say no no longer seem to apply between relatives.
clips.summary: A relative says 'we're family' to shut down your limit or your sense of what is fair, so the closeness becomes a reason you cannot say no.
misuse_warning: Calling every family request 'erasure' can leave you cut off from relatives who simply need help and ask in a clumsy way.
Using the phrase to cover a limit you could have discussed gently can harden a conflict that a calm talk might settle.
clips.safety_note: Usually this is a painful family dynamic and not an emergency. It turns more serious when 'family' is used to get your signature on loans or property, to take your income, or to put children or housing at stake. Before signing anything, speak with a legal aid service or a financial counselor, and keep copies of what you were asked to sign.

clips.name: False Equivalence

beats.hook: Neither of us is perfect.
beats.name: False Equivalence
beats.mechanism: When a large wrong is weighed the same as a small one, the person who was hurt ends up apologizing and the real issue is never fixed. It can also make them doubt their sense of proportion about what happened.
beats.not_this: A conflict in which both people did contribute in a similar degree, and each can name their part in detail.
beats.close: "I do own what I did, and I'm willing to talk about it separately. But what happened with the money is a different size from what I said that night, and I won't call them equal. Let's deal with that one first."

hook_alternates: We both made mistakes here.
We're both equally to blame, honestly.
It takes two people to wreck a marriage.
There's wrong on both sides, so let's call it a draw.
I forgot your birthday, you forgot the trash. We're even.
You raised your voice too, so let's not pretend you're innocent.
clips.short_definition: Presenting very uneven harm as equally shared fault, so that no one is left holding the larger share.
clips.summary: You raise something serious, and the answer is 'we're both at fault', putting a small thing you did on the same scale as a big thing they did.
misuse_warning: Treating every 'we both' as a dodge can make you resist honest self-examination. In many conflicts you do hold a real share, and owning it is a strength.
Using the label to avoid ever being asked about your own part turns an observation into a shield.
clips.safety_note: False Equivalence is not a danger signal by itself, but it can be used to make real harm sound mutual. If the 'both sides' framing is applied to violence, threats, or control of money or contact, a calm talk is not the right place to sort it out. Speak to a domestic abuse advocate or a legal aid service who can look at the full account before you agree to any shared-fault version.

clips.name: Intermittent Reinforcement

beats.hook: "I do love you. You just don't see it."
beats.name: Intermittent Reinforcement
beats.mechanism: Effort goes up while the returns go down. The rarity of the good moments is what makes them feel worth waiting for, so the loop can feed itself, and you may end up measuring the whole relationship by its best hour.
beats.not_this: A relationship with ordinary variation in mood, where kind days are still the large majority.
beats.close: "I've noticed I only hear good things from you once in a while, and I work very hard for those moments. I need steadier warmth, even on ordinary days. If that isn't something you can offer, I'll need to rethink how much I put in."

hook_alternates: "See, this is how it could always be, if you tried a bit harder."
A parent who is cold through most of a visit and then hugs you tightly at the door.
A supervisor who ignores your reports for months and then praises you in front of the team.
Weeks of 'fine' and 'whatever you want,' then one evening of "You're the best thing in my life."
Silence when you do well, and a thank-you only when you stay late or give up something you wanted.
clips.short_definition: Handing out affection, praise or kindness unpredictably and rarely, so that the few good moments hold a person more tightly than steady warmth would.
clips.summary: Kindness shows up only now and then, with no way of knowing when, so you keep working for the next bit and it becomes hard to leave.
misuse_warning: Using the term to describe any uneven mood in a partner can make you read ordinary moodiness as a campaign.
Calling someone's occasional kindness 'just a reward schedule' can dismiss warmth that was real.
clips.safety_note: By itself this is a painful emotional pattern, not a physical danger. Take it more seriously if the gaps are filled with threats, if the warm moments come only after a scare, or if you are tied to the person by money, housing or children. Then keep a record of the cycle and speak to a counselor or advocate who can help you plan your next steps while you still have your own income and contacts.

clips.name: Baiting

beats.hook: There she goes again.
beats.name: Baiting
beats.mechanism: If your reaction is the only part anyone remembers, you can start to distrust your own temper and your own account. It can also cost you at work, in custody talks or with friends, where the reaction is seen and the poke is not.
beats.not_this: A mutual argument in which both people throw barbs and both raise their voices.
beats.close: "That remark landed like a poke, and I'm not going to answer it with a fight. I'm glad to talk about the actual problem. If it turns into poking, we can pause and come back to it in writing."

hook_alternates: Go on, say it. I dare you.
What, are you going to cry now?
I was just asking a question. Why are you screaming?
Calm down. Wow. Everyone can see how unstable this is.
A sly remark about your late father, then a raised eyebrow as your voice rises.
A message timed late at night that gets you to fire back, followed by a screenshot of what you sent.
clips.short_definition: Provoking someone into an angry or upset reaction, then pointing to that reaction as the real problem.
clips.summary: Someone pokes at you until you snap, then points to your reaction as proof that you are the problem.
misuse_warning: Calling any pointed question or blunt remark baiting can excuse your own outbursts. Even when provoked, you remain responsible for how you respond.
Claiming someone baited you because you lost your temper may be true, but the label alone does not show it. It is the repeated sequence that tells the story.
clips.safety_note: Baiting by itself is a trap for your temper, not a physical danger. It matters more if the person uses your reactions in a custody dispute, a workplace complaint or to call the police, or if provocation is followed by violence from them. Keep the full record of what came first, and talk to a lawyer or advocate early.

clips.name: Credibility Theft

beats.hook: You know how she exaggerates.
beats.name: Credibility Theft
beats.mechanism: Your account is discounted before you give it, so whatever you later report meets people who have already been prepared not to believe it, and you may never find out why. Asking for help becomes hardest exactly when you most need it.
beats.not_this: A documented record of inaccuracy reasonably affects how much weight an account carries, and doubting one particular claim is not a campaign. The separation is between doubt about a claim and doubt installed in advance about the person.
beats.close: "I'd like what I report to be looked at on its own facts. I have messages and dates for it. Could we go through them together, or could someone else look at them with us?"

hook_alternates: I'm not saying he's lying, just that he gets confused about dates.
Don't be surprised if he tells you a different story; he does that.
Take what she says with a pinch of salt, she's been going through a lot.
When you report something, the reply opens with 'is this another one of your situations?'
A relative tells the others, 'She'll probably bring that up again, just be kind about it.'
Your manager has already been told you 'tend to misread situations' before you raise your concern.
clips.short_definition: Casting doubt on someone's reliability in advance, so whatever they later report is heard as doubtful before they have said it.
clips.summary: Before you have said anything, other people have been told you exaggerate, get confused or are hard to believe, so what you report lands already doubted.
misuse_warning: Anyone whose account was doubted can feel this has happened to them. A record of real errors reasonably lowers trust, and using the label to wave that record away turns it around.
Confronting the people who repeated the remarks as if they had planned them can look like one more attempt to discredit someone. Check what was actually said, and by whom, before you describe it.
clips.safety_note: This often travels with bigger problems. Watch for doubt being planted with people who decide things about you, such as a landlord, employer, family court or doctor, and for remarks about your mental state used to explain away a report of harm. Keep dated copies somewhere only you can reach, and speak to a legal aid service or an advocate before the next formal step.

clips.name: Demonstrating Omnipotence

beats.hook: I know you stopped at the pharmacy before work.
beats.name: Demonstrating Omnipotence
beats.mechanism: Resistance can stop before anything has been tried, because it has already been made to look pointless. The loss is a choice you never test, and since nothing was tested, you may not notice that it was given up.
beats.not_this: Someone who truly has more information or contacts in one area and uses it openly to help, such as a relative who works at the hospital you are attending.
beats.close: "I want to be the one who decides when my plans get shared. I'm happy to tell you what I'm up to, but I'd rather not go back over how anything was found out." Skip it if you expect anger, and bring the pattern to an advocate instead.

hook_alternates: Funny, I was in your building today. Small world.
You can't surprise me. People tell me everything.
I had a quiet word with your manager. Don't worry about it.
I know people at that school, so I'll hear if anything is wrong.
Whatever you try, I'll hear about it before you've finished doing it.
A photo of you sent with no message, taken somewhere you did not know they were.
clips.short_definition: Showing off how much someone knows, controls or can reach in your life, until trying to act independently starts to look pointless.
clips.summary: Someone keeps showing you how much they know and can do, in ways you never asked for, until trying anything on your own starts to feel useless.
misuse_warning: Reading every coincidence or well-informed friend as proof of surveillance can fuel fear without evidence. Trace one example at a time and check how it was possible.
Using the label for someone who is merely well-connected or boastful treats a personality as a pattern of control.
clips.safety_note: Take it seriously if the displays involve knowing where you are with no explanation, appearing at places you chose to be alone, or references to your children, home or work. Before you raise it or change any settings, check your phone and accounts for tracking with help from a domestic abuse advocate or a technology safety service, since a sudden loss of access can be noticed.

clips.name: Nonverbal Dominance

beats.hook: You ask what is wrong and hear: 'Nothing. I didn't say anything.'
beats.name: Nonverbal Dominance
beats.mechanism: Nothing quotable is said, so the experience is hard to explain to anyone else, and you may end up quietly editing yourself around a reaction you could not describe if asked. Being looked down on, literally, works below the level of argument: you feel smaller and cannot point to why.
beats.not_this: Faces move on their own: a flash of visible irritation, an expressive manner, a real sigh at the end of a long day. The test is whether the reaction appears whenever something is annoying, or specifically whenever one person disagrees.
beats.close: "I can't always tell what a look means, and I would like to hear what you think in words. Could we sit down and each say our piece?"

hook_alternates: When you correct a detail they step closer or lean over your chair.
They turn away or pick up a phone as soon as you mention the budget.
Silent staring after you ask for something, held until you say 'never mind'.
A long exhale and an eye roll the moment you say 'I see it differently', and none when you agree.
They stay standing at the counter looking down at you while you explain, and only sit once you stop talking.
You raise a concern in a meeting and a manager leans back with arms folded, eyes on the ceiling, while others speak without that reaction.
clips.short_definition: Using posture, stares, sighs, eye rolls or the way a body fills a room to dismiss or pressure someone without saying anything.
clips.summary: Without saying a word, someone uses sighs, stares, eye rolls or where they stand to make you feel small, so you stop disagreeing. There is nothing you could quote back to them.
misuse_warning: Reading contempt into every sigh turns ordinary tiredness into an attack. A look is ambiguous; the label needs a repeated link to your disagreement, not one frown.
Accusing someone of dominating a room because of their height or build turns a body into a charge. The pattern is the timing around disagreement, not the body itself.
clips.safety_note: Stares, looming and slow exhales weigh more when they sit beside shouting, broken objects, blocked doorways or being followed from room to room, because the body language can then be a reminder of what has happened before. If you fear the person's reaction, avoid confronting the signals directly. Write down each incident with the date and bring the list to a domestic violence advocate before changing how you respond.

clips.name: Fabricated Evidence

beats.hook: 'I don't need to show you the original. The picture says it all.'
beats.name: Fabricated Evidence
beats.mechanism: Screenshots and documents are widely accepted as proof, so disproving a fake means asking people to doubt evidence they normally trust. Meanwhile your own account can start to look like the lie, and the harm can reach work, school or court before anyone checks the item.
beats.not_this: A real screenshot cropped for brevity, with its meaning intact. Cropping is not forging.
beats.close: "That does not match my records of this conversation. I have the original with its dates saved, and I'd ask that whoever decides this look at both side by side before drawing a conclusion."

hook_alternates: A message under your name, with phrasing or punctuation you never use.
A document that cites an agreement, policy or payment you have never seen or signed.
'Here are the receipts', followed by a screenshot of words you have no memory of writing.
A thread shown to your employer or friends that does not match the same conversation on your own phone.
A screenshot with no way to see the surrounding messages, and a refusal to produce the original phone or an export.
Timestamps, contact names or dates that do not fit when you were actually in touch, or an app layout that does not match the app it claims to come from.
clips.short_definition: Presenting made-up or altered messages, images or documents as genuine proof of something that did not happen or was not said.
clips.summary: Someone shows others a screenshot or document that looks real but was made up or changed, and presents it as proof of something you never wrote, said or did.
misuse_warning: Calling a damaging screenshot fake is the same move reversed: a real record can be disowned with the word 'forged'. Ask for the original, not a verdict.
Telling others that a named person forged something, without evidence, is itself an accusation. Describe which details do not match instead.
clips.safety_note: A fabricated record used in a custody dispute, a protective-order hearing, a workplace complaint or a threat of exposure can cost you housing, income, children or safety, so treat it as a legal matter and not as an argument. Save originals with their dates, delete nothing, and speak to a lawyer or legal aid before replying to the person who produced it. If you fear for your safety, an advocate can help you plan.

clips.name: Synthetic Persona Networks

beats.hook: Accounts with few personal photos, but many opinions on one theme.
beats.name: Synthetic Persona Networks
beats.mechanism: A person forms a view of what others think, or of who they are talking to, from accounts that no real person stands behind. They may change their own opinion, share personal details or join a group on false evidence.
