beats.hook: I don't care, you decide.
beats.name: Strategic Apathy
beats.mechanism: One person makes every decision alone and then carries the criticism for whichever way it went. Over time, deciding stops feeling like having a say and starts feeling like exposure.
beats.not_this: Honest indifference about a small thing, with no later complaint about the outcome.
beats.close: "If you tell me to decide, I'll decide, and then it's decided. I'd like one thing from you before I do. What matters most to you about this? If you really have no preference, I'll go ahead without hearing about it afterward."

hook_alternates: I'm not the one who chose it.
Whatever you want is fine with me.
Do what you want, you always do anyway.
It's your call. Don't blame me if it goes wrong.
(After the choice) Well, I wouldn't have picked that one.
(After the choice) I said I didn't mind, but I didn't think you'd pick that.
clips.short_definition: Declaring 'I don't care' or 'whatever you want' at decision points, then criticizing whichever choice the other person makes.
clips.summary: You are told 'I don't care, you decide', and then whatever you choose turns out to be wrong.
misuse_warning: Reading every 'I don't mind' as a trap can make you miss someone who truly is easygoing. Look for the later criticism, not the shrug.
Pushing a tired or depressed person to state preferences can add to their burden. Ask first whether they are struggling.
clips.safety_note: Strategic Apathy is a pattern about decisions, not a danger in itself. What would change that is blame for outcomes escalating to anger, threats, or punishment, or being left to bear the cost of decisions about money, housing or children with no access to the accounts or papers. If that is happening, collect copies of key documents and speak with a financial counselor or legal aid service about your position.

clips.name: Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde

beats.hook: Warm texts to your family, curt and critical ones to you.
beats.name: Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde
beats.mechanism: You have no witnesses. The version other people know makes your account of the other version sound implausible, including to yourself, and anyone you might turn to has only seen the public one.
beats.not_this: A shy or tired person who is quiet at home and animated at work, with no harshness toward anyone in either place.
beats.close: "I'd like us to speak to each other at home the way we do in front of other people. I'm not asking you to agree about the past, only about how we talk from here."

hook_alternates: "You've got everyone fooled into thinking I'm the bad one."
"No one is going to believe you. Look how everyone sees me."
A friend says, "But he's so lovely whenever I see him. Are you sure?"
A pleasant, joking voice at the party; a flat, hostile one on the drive home.
Affectionate posts and public compliments that rise on the days the private mood is worst.
In front of guests: "Isn't she wonderful? I'd be lost without her." At home, hours later, a cold silence.
clips.short_definition: Showing one warm, admired face to the world and another harsh one to a particular person, which leaves nobody else seeing the treatment that person receives.
clips.summary: Everyone outside the home sees a kind, attentive person. Alone with you, they are cold, controlling or cruel. Because no one else sees it, you wonder who will believe you.
misuse_warning: Calling a person a Jekyll and Hyde because they were short with you after a hard day makes ordinary mood shifts into a case against their character. The label needs a sustained gap, not a bad evening.
Using it to tell friends that a well-liked person is secretly cruel, on the basis of your side alone, can spread a verdict that the evidence cannot yet support.
clips.safety_note: A split like this can sit alongside controlling behavior, threats, or physical harm that stays hidden from outsiders. Warning signs are fear of what happens after guests go home, being told you would not be believed, or having your phone, money or contacts checked. Tell a domestic abuse advocate first, and keep your records somewhere private and out of the home.

clips.name: Weaponized Incompetence

beats.hook: You're just better at it than I am.
beats.name: Weaponized Incompetence
beats.mechanism: The task lands permanently on one person, along with the work of noticing it, asking about it, and eventually giving up on asking. Raising it also makes them sound as if they are complaining about help they were offered.
beats.not_this: A real gap in skill, such as someone who never learned to cook, who is willing to be taught and does improve.
beats.close: "I'm happy to show you how I do the school forms once. After that they're yours to track and finish, including remembering the deadlines. If it turns out to be really hard for you, tell me and we'll work out a swap of equal weight."

hook_alternates: Don't ask me, I never know where anything goes.
I can't work out that form. Could you handle it?
I'll only do it wrong, and then you'll be annoyed.
I loaded the dishwasher and now nothing fits. You'd better do it.
You do it so much faster. It makes sense for you to keep doing it.
A shirt returned pink from the wash, with the remark 'well, I tried'.
clips.short_definition: A pattern in which someone seems unable to do an unwanted task, so that it falls to another person for good.
clips.summary: A chore gets done so badly, or is said to be so hard, that you take it over for good, and it never comes back to them.
misuse_warning: Applying this label to anyone who does a chore differently from you can punish people who are honestly learning or who have a disability. Check whether they improve and whether the load really is uneven.
Using it as an accusation of laziness ends the conversation. This entry is about a pattern in the work, not what anyone intends.
clips.safety_note: This is a fairness and workload issue, not usually a safety one. It changes if the avoided tasks involve a child's medical care or safety, or if you are being punished for handing a task back, or if you control no money and cannot leave a bad split. In those cases, speak to a family doctor, a mediator or legal aid about the specific job at stake.

clips.name: Apology Without Repair

beats.hook: I'm sorry, okay? What more do you want from me?
beats.name: Apology Without Repair
beats.mechanism: Each apology closes the incident without changing anything, so the same harm can recur while, on paper, it has been dealt with every time. The person on the receiving end is left holding a record of apologies and no change.
beats.not_this: A sincere apology followed by imperfect effort. Change is rarely instant and rarely a straight line.
beats.close: "Your apology is real to me, and so is the pattern. This has happened a few times now, so what I need isn't another apology. Can we agree on what will be different next time?"

hook_alternates: I said I was sorry. How many times do I have to say it?
A text reading 'Sorry for everything' that names no action.
It won't happen again, said for the fourth time about the same thing.
I already apologized for that last month. Why are you still going on about it?
I'm so sorry. I hate myself when I do this. (which leaves you comforting them)
A tearful apology, a nice dinner, and the same late arrival the following week.
clips.short_definition: An apology that is offered but followed by no change in behavior, so the same harm returns and the apology closes the matter each time.
clips.summary: They say sorry, sometimes beautifully, and then do the same thing again. After a few rounds the sorry starts to feel like a way of ending the conversation.
misuse_warning: Counting apologies as proof of bad faith is unfair to people working on change slowly. The label fits a closed loop, not a first or second relapse.
It can also be used to refuse any apology, treating sorry as worthless in advance. Sometimes an apology is all that can be offered.
clips.safety_note: An apology followed by repetition can be part of a cycle in controlling or violent relationships, where remorse after an incident is followed by a calm period and then another incident. If the harm involves threats, hitting, destroyed property, control of money, or fear of how they will react, contact a domestic violence advocate, who can help you plan for safety without requiring you to leave. In immediate danger, call emergency services.

clips.name: Complaint Weaponization

beats.hook: "I had to protect myself. Someone had to go to them first."
beats.name: Complaint Weaponization
beats.mechanism: Whichever account reaches the record first tends to set the frame, so a truthful second report is read as a response rather than as information. The person harmed may lose time, credibility, a job or standing before being heard.
beats.not_this: Reporting a real problem quickly through the right channel, which is exactly what people are told to do.
beats.close: "I understand a report was made. I'd like it investigated fairly, and I'd also like my own account looked at as a separate matter, with the dates of what happened set out in writing."

hook_alternates: "Funny that you're only bringing this up now, after I reported you."
A formal letter listing your faults, sent a day after a heated argument with no earlier warning.
"I've already spoken to HR about the way you treated me." (said before you have contacted anyone)
A mutual friend saying, "She told the group leader first, so I'm not sure it's wise to push this."
A manager telling you, "There's already a complaint about you on file. Anything you raise now will be looked at in that light."
clips.short_definition: Using a formal or informal complaint, often filed first, to shape how a later and truthful report from the other person will be received.
clips.summary: Someone files a complaint about you first, so that when you report what really happened, it looks like revenge instead of a first account.
misuse_warning: Using this label against someone who reported first, in good faith, can discourage people from reporting real problems.
Saying 'you filed first so you must be doing this' treats timing as proof, and timing alone does not show it.
clips.safety_note: A complaint can put your income, housing, custody of children or immigration status at risk, so treat a surprise filing as more serious than an ordinary dispute. Watch for threats to report you if you speak, or a deadline to respond. Get your own dated records together at once and contact an employment lawyer, tenant advocate, legal aid clinic or union representative before replying.

clips.name: Forced Forgiveness

beats.hook: Can we just move past this?
beats.name: Forced Forgiveness
beats.mechanism: Resolution is claimed before acknowledgment, so the harm stays unprocessed. Any further mention of it then becomes the new problem, and the person who was hurt carries the extra task of looking forgiving.
beats.not_this: A mutual decision to move forward after real acknowledgment has happened. That is repair, not pressure.
beats.close: "I'd like things to be better between us. Before I can forgive, I need what happened to be acknowledged, and I can't rush that. Please don't ask me again for now. I'll tell you when I'm ready."

hook_alternates: Everyone else has moved on. Why can't you?
It's been long enough. You need to let it go.
He's family. Life's too short to hold grudges.
Forgiveness is what God asks of us, and you're holding on.
I've said I'm sorry. Now you have to forgive me. That's how it works.
If you really cared about this family, you'd shake his hand at the wedding.
clips.short_definition: Pressing someone to forgive or move on before the harm has been acknowledged or made right, so forgiveness is demanded in place of repair.
clips.summary: The people around you want it over. You are told to forgive and move on though no one has faced what happened, and still feeling hurt is treated as the problem.
misuse_warning: Telling anyone who urges peace that they are 'forcing forgiveness' can silence people who sincerely want to help, or who are themselves hurt by the rift.
The label can harden into a rule that forgiveness must never be asked of anyone. A gentle invitation is not coercion.
clips.safety_note: Pressure to forgive can keep a person in contact with someone who hurt them, which matters most when the harm was violence, abuse or threats. Forgiving in your heart does not oblige you to see anyone or be alone with them. If you are being pushed to go back to a person you fear, a domestic violence or sexual assault advocate can help you plan how to say no and stay safe. In immediate danger, call emergency services.

clips.name: Plausible Deniability

beats.hook: I was just being honest.
beats.name: Plausible Deniability
beats.mechanism: Every incident comes with a fair-sounding explanation, so raising any one of them can make the person raising it look unreasonable. The pattern can only be described by pointing at things that, taken separately, look like nothing.
beats.not_this: People do follow policy and do worry about others. Often the innocent explanation is simply the true one.
beats.close: "I believe you may have good reasons each time, and I'm not asking you to prove them. Could we think about how messages and accounts are handled, with a third person there? I would feel better that way." Offer it only when you judge it safe; if not, take the list to an advocate first.

hook_alternates: It's just policy. My hands are tied.
It was a joke. Where's your sense of humor?
I didn't mean it that way. You're reading into it.
I never told you not to go. I just said I'd be upset.
Nobody said you couldn't. We just thought it would look bad.
I was only worried about you. That's why I read your messages.
I must have forgotten to tell you about the change to your shifts.
clips.short_definition: Acting in ways that can always be explained as concern, policy or accident, so no single incident can be called harmful without the accuser sounding unfair.
clips.summary: Every time something harmful happens, there is a decent-sounding reason, so you can never point to one thing without feeling unfair. Only the whole pile shows the shape.
misuse_warning: Not every explanation is a cover story. Treating all reasons as cover makes honest explanation impossible and makes the label impossible to disprove.
Because the term describes a pattern, using it on a single incident turns an ambiguous event into an accusation it cannot support.
clips.safety_note: Concern and rules are a common explanation for controlling behavior such as reading your messages, tracking your location, holding your documents, or limiting your contact with friends and money. If the explanations lead to you losing access to those things, or you fear the response to questions, take your dated list to a domestic abuse advocate or, at work, an employment lawyer. Keep copies of key documents somewhere safe outside the situation.

clips.name: Victim Role Reversal

beats.hook: "I can't handle this right now. I need you to be supportive."
beats.name: Victim Role Reversal
beats.mechanism: Sympathy that should have gone to the person harmed goes elsewhere, and the person harmed ends up soothing and apologizing. Onlookers form an impression that is very hard to correct later, and the person harmed may start doubting whether they have the right to be upset.
beats.not_this: Two people who were both hurt in the same conflict, each with a fair claim to be heard.
beats.close: "I'm sorry you're hurting, and I want to hear about it later. Right now I need you to hear what happened from my side first. After that, I will listen as long as you need."

hook_alternates: "I'm the one everyone piles onto. Nobody ever asks how I'm doing."
"I guess I'm just a terrible person, then. Is that what you want me to say?"
You, a few minutes after you were the one wronged: "I'm sorry I brought it up."
"Do you have any idea how hard this has been for me?" (after you raised what they did)
"After everything I've done, this is how I'm treated? I'm the one who's been hurt here."
Tearful silence and withdrawal as soon as the complaint is named, followed by you finding yourself offering a hug.
A mutual friend saying, "I just don't think you realize how much you've hurt them." (about the person who raised the complaint)
clips.short_definition: Presenting oneself as the injured party when asked to answer for harm, so that sympathy and comforting move away from the person who was actually hurt.
clips.summary: After hurting you, they become the one who is hurt, and you, and maybe everyone around you, end up looking after them while what happened to you drops out of the room.
misuse_warning: Calling every upset reaction 'victim reversal' can make you deaf to someone who really is hurt, including in a conflict where both of you hurt each other.
Saying it to a person in tears, in the middle of the argument, tends to turn a description into an accusation.
clips.safety_note: This pattern alone is not a physical-safety concern. It changes when the person who is 'hurt' also says they will harm themselves if you pull back, spreads the story to cut you off from friends, or uses it to shape custody or workplace decisions. Keep a dated record of what was said and who heard it, and contact a crisis line about any self-harm statement, or a legal aid service about custody or work.
